title.zh: 卷三百十二 列傳第七十一 韓琦子:忠彥 曾公亮子:孝寬 孝廣 孝蘊 陳升之 吳充 王珪從父:罕 從兄:琪
title.en: Volume 312 Biographies 71: Han Qi and son: Zhongyan, Ceng Gongliang and son: Xiaokuan, Xiao Guang, Xiao Yun, Chen Shengzhi, Wu Chong, Wang Gui and uncle: Han, nephew: Qi
title.raw: 卷三百十二 列傳第七十一 韓琦子:忠彥 曾公亮子:孝寬 孝廣 孝蘊 陳升之 吳充 王珪從父:罕 從兄:琪 Volume 312 Biographies 71: Han Qi and son: Zhongyan, Ceng Gongliang and son: Xiaokuan, Xiao Guang, Xiao Yun, Chen Shengzhi, Wu Chong, Wang Gui and uncle: Han, nephew: Qi

sentences.zh: 韓琦，字稚圭，相州安陽人。

translations.literal: Han Qi, styled Zhigui, was a man of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi, styled Zhigui, was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父國華，自有傳。

translations.literal: His father Guohua has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guohua has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 琦風骨秀異，弱冠舉進士，名在第二。

translations.literal: Qi had an outstanding bearing and exceptional presence; in his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination, ranking second.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had a striking presence and exceptional bearing; in his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination, placing second.

sentences.zh: 方唱名，太史奏日下五色雲見，左右皆賀。

translations.literal: As his name was being called forth, the court astronomer reported that five-colored clouds had appeared beneath the sun, and all those around offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: As his name was being announced, the court astronomer reported five-colored clouds beneath the sun, and everyone around him offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 授將作監丞、通判淄州，入直集賢院、監左藏庫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and concurrent magistrate of Zizhou, entered service in the Hall of Assembled Talents, and supervised the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and concurrent magistrate of Zizhou, took up duty in the Hall of Assembled Talents, and supervised the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 時方貴高科，多徑去為顯職，琦獨滯筦庫，眾以為非宜，琦處之自若。

translations.literal: At the time high examination honors were prized and many went straight to prominent posts; Qi alone remained stuck in the treasury, which people thought inappropriate, but Qi took it calmly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time top examination honors were highly prized and many went straight into prominent posts; Qi alone lingered in the treasury, which people thought unfitting, yet he remained entirely at ease.

sentences.zh: 禁中需金帛，皆內臣直批旨取之，無印可驗，琦請復舊制，置傳宣合同司，以相防察。

translations.literal: When the palace needed gold and silks, eunuchs took them directly by written order with no seal to verify; Qi requested restoration of the old system and establishment of a Transmit-and-Proclaim Contract Office for mutual oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the palace needed gold and silks, eunuchs took them on direct written orders with no seal to verify; Qi asked that the old system be restored and a Transmit-and-Proclaim Contract Office set up so the two sides could check each other.

sentences.zh: 又每綱運至，必俟內臣監蒞，始得受，往往數日不至，暴露廡下，衙校以為病，琦奏罷之。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever convoy shipments arrived they had to wait for eunuch supervision before acceptance, often not arriving for days and leaving goods exposed under the portico; clerks considered this harmful and Qi memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whenever convoy shipments arrived they had to wait for eunuch overseers before they could be received; the overseers often did not come for days, and goods lay exposed under the portico. The clerks regarded this as a serious abuse, and Qi memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官、三司度支判官，拜右司諫。

translations.literal: He served successively as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture and fiscal judge of the Three Departments, and was appointed Remonstrator of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture and fiscal judge of the Three Departments, and was appointed remonstrator of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時宰相王隨、陳堯佐，參知政事韓億、石中立，在中書罕所建明，琦連疏其過，四人同日罷。

translations.literal: At the time the chief ministers Wang Sui and Chen Yaozuo and vice commissioners Han Yi and Shi Zhongli rarely proposed policies in the Secretariat; Qi submitted successive memorials on their faults and all four were dismissed the same day.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief ministers Wang Sui and Chen Yaozuo and the vice commissioners Han Yi and Shi Zhongli seldom put forward policy in the Secretariat; Qi submitted successive memorials detailing their faults, and all four were dismissed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 又請停內降，抑僥倖。

translations.literal: He also requested suspension of palace directives and curbing of favor-seeking.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that palace directives be halted and favor-seeking curbed.

sentences.zh: 凡事有不便，未嘗不言，每以明得失、正紀綱、親忠直、遠邪佞為急，前後七十餘疏。

translations.literal: Whenever anything was inconvenient he spoke out; he always made it urgent to clarify gains and losses, rectify discipline, draw near the loyal and upright, and keep the wicked and fawning at distance—over seventy memorials in all.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anything was amiss he spoke out; he always pressed to clarify what worked and what failed, set discipline right, draw the loyal and upright close, and keep the wicked and fawning at a distance—more than seventy memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 王曾為相，謂之曰：「今言者不激，則多畏顧，何補上德？

translations.literal: When Wang Zeng was chief minister he said to him: "Nowadays remonstrators who are not forceful mostly fear and hold back—how does that aid the sovereign's virtue?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zeng was chief minister he said to him, "Nowadays remonstrators who are not forceful mostly fear consequences and hold back—how does that serve the sovereign's virtue?

sentences.zh: 如君言，可謂切而不迂矣。

translations.literal: Words like yours may be called pointed yet not pedantic."
translations.idiomatic: What you say may be called pointed without being pedantic."

sentences.zh: 」曾聞望方崇，罕所獎與，琦聞其語，益自信。

translations.literal: Zeng's reputation was then at its height and he rarely offered praise; when Qi heard these words he grew all the more confident.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng's reputation was then at its height and he rarely offered praise; when Qi heard this he grew all the more confident in himself.

sentences.zh: 權知制誥。

translations.literal: He served as acting commissioner for drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting commissioner for drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 益、利歲饑，為體量安撫使。

translations.literal: When Yi and Li circuits suffered famine in successive years, he was made commissioner for assessing and pacifying the region.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi and Li circuits suffered famine year after year, he was appointed commissioner for assessing and pacifying the region.

sentences.zh: 異時郡縣督賦調繁急，市上供綺繡諸物不予直，琦為緩調蠲給之，逐貪殘不職吏，汰冗役數百，活饑民百九十萬。

translations.literal: In former times prefectures and counties pressed tax levies harshly and urgently; goods such as silks and embroideries supplied to the market were not paid fair value. Qi eased levies and granted relief, expelled greedy and cruel officials who neglected duty, eliminated several hundred superfluous corvée posts, and kept alive 1.9 million famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: In former times prefectures and counties had pressed tax levies harshly; silks and embroideries and other goods supplied to the market were not paid fair value. Qi eased the levies and granted relief, expelled greedy and cruel officials who neglected their duties, cut several hundred superfluous corvée posts, and kept alive 1.9 million people stricken by famine.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊反，琦適自蜀歸，論西師形勢甚悉，即命為陝西安撫使。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, Qi had just returned from Shu and discussed the western army's situation very thoroughly; he was immediately appointed pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, Qi had just returned from Shu and discussed the western army's situation in full detail; he was immediately appointed pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 劉平與賊戰，敗，為所執，時宰入他誣，收繫平子弟，琦辨直其冤。

translations.literal: Liu Ping fought the rebels, was defeated, and captured; the chief ministers accepted other slanders, arrested and imprisoned Ping's sons and younger brothers, and Qi argued to clear his wrongful conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping fought the rebels, was defeated, and taken captive; the chief ministers accepted other slanders and arrested Ping's sons and younger brothers; Qi argued his case and cleared the wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士，副夏竦為經略安撫、招討使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and served as deputy to Xia Song as commissioner for frontier pacification and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and served as deputy to Xia Song as frontier pacification and suppression commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使督出兵，琦亦欲先發以制賊，而合府固爭，元昊遂寇鎮戎。

translations.literal: An edict sent envoys to supervise troop deployment; Qi also wished to strike first to control the rebels, but the whole headquarters stubbornly argued against it, and Yuanhao then raided Zhenrong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent envoys to supervise troop movements; Qi also wanted to strike first and seize the initiative, but the whole headquarters stubbornly opposed him, and Yuanhao then raided Zhenrong.

sentences.zh: 琦畫攻守二策馳入奏，仁宗欲用攻策，執政者難之，琦言：「元昊雖傾國入寇，眾不過四五萬人，吾逐路重兵自為守，勢分力弱，遇敵輒不支。

translations.literal: Qi drew up offensive and defensive strategies and rushed them in memorial; Emperor Renzong wished to adopt the offensive plan but the chief administrators found it difficult. Qi said: "Although Yuanhao has thrown the whole state into invasion, his forces number no more than forty or fifty thousand; we keep heavy troops on each route merely to defend ourselves, our strength is divided and weak, and whenever we meet the enemy we cannot hold."
translations.idiomatic: Qi drew up offensive and defensive plans and rushed them to court; Emperor Renzong wished to adopt the offensive plan but the chief administrators balked. Qi said, "Although Yuanhao has thrown his whole state into the invasion, his forces number no more than forty or fifty thousand; we keep heavy troops on each route merely to hold our own ground, our strength is divided and weak, and whenever we meet the enemy we cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 若倂出一道，鼓行而前，乘賊驕惰，破之必矣。

translations.literal: If we unite on one route and advance with drums beating, taking advantage of the rebels' arrogance and slackness, we will surely break them."
translations.idiomatic: If we unite on a single route and advance with drums beating, taking advantage of the rebels' arrogance and slackness, we are sure to break them."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔鄜延、涇原同出征。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Fuyan and Jingyuan circuits to campaign together.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the Fuyan and Jingyuan circuits to campaign together.

sentences.zh: 既還營，元昊來求盟，琦曰：「無約而請和者，謀也。

translations.literal: After returning to camp Yuanhao came seeking alliance; Qi said: "One who seeks peace without a prior agreement is plotting."
translations.idiomatic: After returning to camp Yuanhao came seeking peace; Qi said, "Anyone who seeks peace without a prior agreement is plotting."

sentences.zh: 」命諸將戒嚴，賊果犯山外。

translations.literal: He ordered the generals to stand on alert, and the rebels indeed attacked outside the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the generals to stand on alert, and the rebels did indeed attack beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 琦悉兵付大將任福，令自懷遠城趨德勝砦出賊後，如未可戰，即據險置伏，要其歸。

translations.literal: Qi entrusted all troops to the great general Ren Fu, ordering him to march from Huaiyuan city toward Desheng fort and emerge behind the rebels; if battle was not yet feasible, he was to seize difficult ground, set ambushes, and intercept their return.
translations.idiomatic: Qi entrusted all the troops to the great general Ren Fu, ordering him to march from Huaiyuan city toward Desheng fort and come out behind the rebels; if battle was not yet feasible, he was to hold difficult ground, set ambushes, and cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 及行，戒之至再。

translations.literal: When he set out, Qi admonished him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu set out, Qi admonished him again and again.

sentences.zh: 又移檄申約，苟違節度，雖有功，亦斬。

translations.literal: He also sent a written order restating the agreement: if anyone violated command, even with merit he would be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a written order restating the agreement: anyone who violated command would be executed, even if he had merit.

sentences.zh: 福竟為賊誘，沒于好水川。

translations.literal: Fu was ultimately lured by the rebels and perished at Hao River.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was ultimately lured into a trap by the rebels and perished at Hao River.

sentences.zh: 竦使人收散兵，得琦檄於福衣帶間，言罪不在琦。

translations.literal: Xia Song sent men to gather the scattered troops and found Qi's order in Fu's belt, stating that the fault did not lie with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song sent men to gather the scattered troops and found Qi's order in Fu's belt, stating that the blame did not lie with Qi.

sentences.zh: 琦亦上章自劾，猶奪一官，知秦州，尋復之。

translations.literal: Qi also submitted a memorial impeaching himself; he still lost one rank, was made prefect of Qinzhou, and soon had it restored.
translations.idiomatic: Qi also submitted a memorial impeaching himself; he still lost one rank, was made prefect of Qinzhou, and soon had it restored.

sentences.zh: 會四路置帥，以琦兼秦鳳經略安撫、招討使。

translations.literal: When commanders were appointed for the four circuits, Qi was made concurrently frontier pacification and suppression commissioner of Qinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When commanders were appointed for the four circuits, Qi was made concurrently frontier pacification and suppression commissioner of Qinfeng.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，與三帥皆換觀察使，范仲淹、龐籍、王沿不肯拜，琦獨受不辭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingli, he and the three commanders were all transferred to observer commissioner posts; Fan Zhongyan, Pang Ji, and Wang Yan refused to accept, but Qi alone accepted without demur.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingli he and the three commanders were all transferred to observer commissioner posts; Fan Zhongyan, Pang Ji, and Wang Yan refused to accept, but Qi alone accepted without demur.

sentences.zh: 未幾，還舊職，為陝西四路經略安撫、招討使，屯涇州。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his former post as frontier pacification and suppression commissioner of the four Shaanxi circuits, stationed at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to his former post as frontier pacification and suppression commissioner of the four Shaanxi circuits, stationed at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 琦與范仲淹在兵間久，名重一時，人心歸之，朝廷倚以為重，故天下稱為「韓范」。

translations.literal: Qi and Fan Zhongyan had long been among the troops; their fame weighed on the age, hearts turned to them, and the court relied on them as a heavy weight—so the realm called them "Han and Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Fan Zhongyan had long been in the field; their fame weighed on the age, hearts turned to them, and the court relied on them heavily—so the realm called them "Han and Fan."

sentences.zh: 東兵從宿衛來，不習勞苦，琦奏增土兵以代戍，建德順軍以蔽蕭關、嗚沙之道。

translations.literal: Eastern troops coming from palace guard service were unused to hardship; Qi memorialized to increase local troops to replace garrison duty and established the Deshun army to screen the routes of Xiaoguan and Wusha.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern troops coming from palace guard service were unused to hardship; Qi memorialized to increase local troops to replace garrison duty and established the Deshun army to screen the routes through Xiaoguan and Wusha.

sentences.zh: 方謀取橫山，規河南，而元昊稱臣，召為樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was just planning to take Hengshan and target the region south of the river when Yuanhao submitted as a vassal and Qi was summoned as vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was just planning to take Hengshan and target the region south of the river when Yuanhao submitted as a vassal and Qi was summoned as vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元昊介契丹為援，強邀索無厭，宰相晏殊等厭兵，將一切從之。

translations.literal: Yuanhao relied on the Khitan as support and pressed demands without end; chief minister Yan Shu and others were weary of war and were about to yield on everything.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao relied on Khitan support and pressed demands without end; chief minister Yan Shu and others were weary of war and were about to yield on everything.

sentences.zh: 琦陳其不便，條所宜先行者七事：一曰清政本，二曰念邊計，三曰擢材賢，四曰備河北，五曰固河東，六曰收民心，七曰營洛邑。

translations.literal: Qi set forth the drawbacks and listed seven matters that should be undertaken first: first, clarify the foundation of government; second, heed frontier planning; third, promote worthy talent; fourth, prepare Hebei; fifth, secure Hedong; sixth, win the people's hearts; seventh, build the Luo capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qi set forth the drawbacks and listed seven matters that should be undertaken first: clarify the foundation of government; heed frontier planning; promote worthy talent; prepare Hebei; secure Hedong; win the people's hearts; and build the Luo capital.

sentences.zh: 繼又陳救弊八事，欲選將帥，明按察，豐財利，遏僥倖，進能吏，退不才，謹入官，去冗食。

translations.literal: He then set forth eight measures to remedy abuses: select generals and commanders, clarify inspection, enrich finances, curb favor-seeking, advance capable officials, dismiss the untalented, tighten entry into office, and remove superfluous consumption.
translations.idiomatic: He then set forth eight measures to remedy abuses: select generals and commanders, clarify inspection, enrich finances, curb favor-seeking, advance capable officials, dismiss the untalented, tighten entry into office, and remove superfluous consumption.

sentences.zh: 謂：「數者之舉，謗必隨之，願委計輔臣，聽其注措。

translations.literal: He said: "When such measures are undertaken, slander is sure to follow; I hope Your Majesty will entrust the plan to supporting ministers and let them carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "When such measures are undertaken, slander is sure to follow; I hope Your Majesty will entrust the plan to your supporting ministers and let them carry it out."

sentences.zh: 」帝悉嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and accepted all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and accepted all of them.

sentences.zh: 遂宣撫陝西，討平群盜張海、郭邈山；

translations.literal: He was then made pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and suppressed the bandit chiefs Zhang Hai and Guo Miaoshan;
translations.idiomatic: He was then made pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and suppressed the bandit chiefs Zhang Hai and Guo Miaoshan;

sentences.zh: 禁卒羸老不任用者，悉汰之；

translations.literal: palace guards who were weak, old, and unfit for service were all eliminated;
translations.idiomatic: palace guards who were weak, old, and unfit for service were all eliminated;

sentences.zh: 盡修鄜延城障，須敵悉歸所侵地，乃許和。

translations.literal: he fully repaired the fortifications of Fuyan circuit and would permit peace only when the enemy had wholly returned all seized territory.
translations.idiomatic: he fully repaired the fortifications of Fuyan circuit and would permit peace only when the enemy had wholly returned all seized territory.

sentences.zh: 歸陳西北四策，以為：「今當以和好為權宜，戰守為實務。

translations.literal: On his return he set forth four strategies for the northwest, holding that: "For the present we should take peace as an expedient and fighting and defense as the real task.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he set forth four strategies for the northwest, arguing that for the present peace should be treated as an expedient while fighting and defense remained the real task.

sentences.zh: 請繕甲厲兵，營修都城，密定討伐之計。」

translations.literal: I ask that armor be repaired, troops sharpened, the capital fortified, and plans for campaign secretly settled."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that armor be repaired, troops sharpened, the capital fortified, and plans for campaign settled in secret."

sentences.zh: 時二府合班奏事，琦必盡言，雖事屬中書，亦指陳其實。

translations.literal: At the time the Two Departments reported together in court audience; Qi always spoke fully, and even when a matter belonged to the Secretariat he would point out how things really stood.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Two Departments reported together in court audience; Qi always spoke his mind fully, and even when a matter belonged to the Secretariat he would point out how things really stood.

sentences.zh: 同列或不悅，帝獨識之，曰：「韓琦性直。

translations.literal: Colleagues were sometimes displeased, but the emperor alone understood him and said: "Han Qi is by nature straightforward."
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues were sometimes displeased, but the emperor alone understood him and said, "Han Qi is by nature straightforward."

sentences.zh: 」琦與范仲淹、富弼皆以海內人望，同時登用，中外跂想其勳業。

translations.literal: Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi were all men of renown throughout the realm, appointed at the same time; within and without the court all looked eagerly to their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi were all men of renown throughout the realm and were appointed at the same time; within and without the court all looked eagerly to their achievements.

sentences.zh: 仲淹等亦以天下為己任，群小不便之，毀言日聞。

translations.literal: Fan and the others also took the realm as their own charge; petty men found this inconvenient and slander was heard daily.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and the others also took the realm as their own charge; petty men found this inconvenient, and slander was heard daily.

sentences.zh: 仲淹、弼繼罷，琦為辨析，不報。

translations.literal: Fan and Fu were dismissed in succession; Qi argued to clarify their case but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Fu were dismissed in succession; Qi argued to clarify their case but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 尹洙與劉滬爭城水洛事，琦右洙，朝論不謂然。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu and Liu Hu disputed the fortification of Shuiluo; Qi sided with Zhu, and court opinion did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu and Liu Hu disputed the fortification of Shuiluo; Qi sided with Zhu, and court opinion did not agree.

sentences.zh: 乃請外，以資政殿學士知揚州，徙鄆州、成德軍、定州。

translations.literal: He then requested an outside post, was made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Yangzhou, and was transferred to Yanzhou, the Chengde army, and Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested an outside post, was made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Yangzhou, and was transferred to Yanzhou, the Chengde army, and Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 兼安撫使，進大學士，又加觀文殿學士。

translations.literal: He was also made pacification commissioner, promoted to grand academician, and further given the title of academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made pacification commissioner, promoted to grand academician, and further given the title of academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture.

sentences.zh: 初，定州兵狃平貝州功，需賞賚，出怨語，至欲噪城下。

translations.literal: At first the Dingzhou troops, accustomed to the merit of pacifying Beizhou, demanded rewards, uttered resentful words, and even wished to riot beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Dingzhou troops, accustomed to the glory of pacifying Beizhou, demanded rewards, uttered resentful words, and even wished to riot beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 琦聞之，以為不治且亂，用軍制勒習，誅其尤無良者。

translations.literal: When Qi heard of this he thought that if not corrected there would soon be disorder; he applied military regulations to compel drill and executed the worst offenders.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi heard of this he thought that if the matter were not corrected there would soon be disorder; he applied military regulations to compel drill and executed the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 士死攻戰，則賞賻其家，籍其孤嫠繼稟之，威恩並行。

translations.literal: When soldiers died in attack or battle he rewarded their families, registered their orphans and widows and continued their rations, combining sternness and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers died in attack or battle he rewarded their families, registered their orphans and widows and continued their rations, combining sternness and kindness.

sentences.zh: 又仿古三陣法，日月訓齊之，由是中山兵精勁冠河朔。

translations.literal: He also modeled the ancient three-formations method and trained them day by day until they were in step; thereby the Zhongshan troops became the finest and strongest north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He also modeled the ancient three-formations method and trained them day by day until they moved as one; thereby the Zhongshan troops became the finest and strongest north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 京師發龍猛卒戍保州，在道為人害，至定，琦悉留不遣，易素教者使之北，又振活饑民數百萬。

translations.literal: The capital sent Longmeng guards to garrison Baozhou; on the road they harmed people, and when they reached Dingzhou Qi kept them all and would not send them on, exchanging plain and tractable men to send north; he also revived several million famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: The capital sent Longmeng guards to garrison Baozhou; on the road they harmed people, and when they reached Dingzhou Qi kept them all and would not send them on, exchanging plain and tractable men to send north; he also revived several million people stricken by famine.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒激，鄰道視以為準。

translations.literal: Imperial letters praised and encouraged him, and neighboring circuits took him as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial letters praised and encouraged him, and neighboring circuits took him as their standard.

sentences.zh: 拜武康軍節度使、知幷州。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of the Wukang army and prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Wukang army and prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 承受廖浩然，怙中貴勢貪恣，既誣逐前帥李昭亮，所為益不法，琦奏還之，帝命鞭諸本省。

translations.literal: The receiver Liao Haoran relied on eunuch power, was greedy and unrestrained, had already slandered and driven out the former commander Li Zhaoliang, and his conduct grew still more lawless; Qi memorialized to have him returned and the emperor ordered him flogged at the relevant bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The receiver Liao Haoran relied on eunuch power, was greedy and unrestrained, had already slandered and driven out the former commander Li Zhaoliang, and his conduct grew still more lawless; Qi memorialized to have him recalled and the emperor ordered him flogged at the relevant bureau.

sentences.zh: 契丹冒占天池廟地，琦召其酋豪，示以曩日彼所求修廟檄，無以對，遂歸我斥地。

translations.literal: The Khitan encroached on and seized Tianchi Temple land; Qi summoned their chieftains and showed them the petition they had once submitted to repair the temple—they had no answer and returned our expelled territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan encroached on and seized Tianchi Temple land; Qi summoned their chieftains and showed them the petition they had once submitted to repair the temple—they had no answer and returned the land we had been forced to yield.

sentences.zh: 既又侵耕陽武砦地，琦鑿塹立石以限之。

translations.literal: They then also encroached on farmland at Yangwu stockade; Qi dug trenches and set up stones to mark the limit.
translations.idiomatic: They then also encroached on farmland at Yangwu stockade; Qi dug trenches and set up boundary stones to mark the limit.

sentences.zh: 始，潘美鎮河東，患寇鈔，令民悉內徙，而空塞下不耕，於是忻、代、寧化、大山之北多廢壤。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Pan Mei held Hedong, fearing bandit raids he ordered the people all to move inward, leaving the frontier empty and untilled; thus north of Xin, Dai, Ninghua, and Dashan there was much abandoned land.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, when Pan Mei held Hedong, fearing bandit raids he ordered the people all to move inward, leaving the frontier empty and untilled; thus north of Xin, Dai, Ninghua, and Dashan there was much abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 琦以為此皆良田，今棄不耕，適足以資敵，將皆為所有矣。

translations.literal: Qi held that all this was fine farmland; now abandoned and untilled, it would only supply the enemy and in time all would become theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Qi held that all this was fine farmland; abandoned and left untilled, it would only supply the enemy, and in time all would become theirs.

sentences.zh: 遂請距北界十里為禁地，其南則募弓箭手居之，墾田至九千六百頃。

translations.literal: He then requested that within ten li of the northern border be forbidden ground, and south of that archers be recruited to settle; land opened reached 9,600 qing.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested that within ten li of the northern border be forbidden ground, and south of that archers be recruited to settle; land brought under cultivation reached 9,600 qing.

sentences.zh: 久之，求知相州。

translations.literal: After a long while he requested appointment as prefect of his home Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he requested appointment as prefect of his home Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年，召為三司使，未至，迎拜樞密使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiayou he was summoned as commissioner of the Three Departments; before he arrived he was met and appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiayou he was summoned as commissioner of the Three Departments; before he arrived he was met on the road and appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，拜同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Tongzhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi rank and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year he was appointed grand councilor of the Tongzhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi rank and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents.

sentences.zh: 六年閏八月，遷昭文館大學士、監修國史，封儀國公。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month of the sixth year he was transferred to grand academician of the Hall of Illustrious Literature and supervisor of compiling the national history, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month of the sixth year he was transferred to grand academician of the Hall of Illustrious Literature and supervisor of compiling the national history, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝既連失三王，自至和中病疾，不能御殿。

translations.literal: The emperor had already lost three princes in succession; from the Zhihe era he was ill and could not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already lost three princes in succession; from the Zhihe era he was ill and could not hold court.

sentences.zh: 中外惴恐，臣下爭以立嗣固根本為言，包拯、范鎮尤激切。

translations.literal: Within and without the court all were fearful; officials vied to speak of establishing an heir to secure the foundation, Bao Zheng and Fan Zhen especially forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court all were fearful; officials vied to speak of establishing an heir to secure the foundation, Bao Zheng and Fan Zhen especially forceful.

sentences.zh: 積五六歲，依違未之行，言者亦稍怠。

translations.literal: For five or six years the matter dragged on without action, and those who spoke also gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: For five or six years the matter dragged on without action, and those who spoke also gradually slackened.

sentences.zh: 至是，琦乘間進曰：「皇嗣者，天下安危之所系。

translations.literal: At this point Qi seized an opening and advanced: "The imperial heir is what the realm's safety and peril depend upon.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Qi seized an opening and said, "The imperial heir is what the realm's safety and peril depend upon.

sentences.zh: 自昔禍亂之起，皆由策不早定。

translations.literal: From of old the rise of calamity and disorder has all been because the plan was not settled early.
translations.idiomatic: From of old calamity and disorder have arisen because the plan was not settled early.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋高，未有建立，何不擇宗室之賢者，以為宗廟社稷計？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years are advanced and no heir has yet been established—why not select a worthy member of the imperial clan for the sake of the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's years are advanced and no heir has yet been established—why not select a worthy member of the imperial clan for the sake of the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「後宮將有就館者，姑待之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Someone in the inner palace is about to enter confinement—let us wait for now."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Someone in the inner palace is about to enter confinement—let us wait for now."

sentences.zh: 」已又生女。

translations.literal: Soon afterward another daughter was born.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward another daughter was born.

sentences.zh: 一日，琦懷《漢書·孔光傳》以進，曰：「成帝無嗣，立弟之子。

translations.literal: One day Qi brought in the Biography of Kong Guang in the Book of Han and advanced: "Emperor Cheng had no heir and established his younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: One day Qi brought in the Biography of Kong Guang in the Book of Han and said, "Emperor Cheng had no heir and established his younger brother's son.

sentences.zh: 彼中材之主，猶能如是，況陛下乎。

translations.literal: That was a ruler of only middling talent, yet he could act thus—how much more Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: That was a ruler of only middling talent, yet he could act thus—how much more can Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 願以太祖之心為心，則無不可者。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will take Taizu's heart as your own heart—then nothing will be impossible."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will take Taizu's heart as your own heart—then nothing will be impossible."

sentences.zh: 」又與曾公亮、張昇、歐陽修極言之。

translations.literal: He also spoke to the utmost on the matter with Zeng Gongliang, Zhang Sheng, and Ouyang Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke to the utmost on the matter with Zeng Gongliang, Zhang Sheng, and Ouyang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 會司馬光、呂誨皆有請，琦進讀二疏，未及有所啟，帝遽曰：「朕有意久矣，誰可者？

translations.literal: When Sima Guang and Lü Hui both made requests, Qi advanced to read the two memorials; before he could speak further the emperor suddenly said: "I have had this in mind for a long time—who would be suitable?"
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang and Lü Hui both made requests, Qi advanced to read the two memorials; before he could speak further the emperor suddenly said, "I have had this in mind for a long time—who would be suitable?"

sentences.zh: 」琦皇恐對曰：「此非臣輩所可議，當出自聖擇。

translations.literal: Qi answered in fear and trembling: "This is not something we ministers may discuss—it should come from Your Majesty's own choice."
translations.idiomatic: Qi answered in fear and trembling, "This is not something we ministers may discuss—it should come from Your Majesty's own choice."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「宮中嘗養二子，小者甚純，近不慧，大者可也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The palace once raised two sons; the younger is very pure-hearted but lately has not been clever—the elder will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The palace once raised two sons; the younger is very pure-hearted but lately has not been clever—the elder will do."

sentences.zh: 」琦請其名，帝以宗實告。

translations.literal: Qi asked his name and the emperor told him Zongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi asked his name and the emperor told him Zongshi.

sentences.zh: 宗實，英宗舊名也。

translations.literal: Zongshi was Yingzong's former name.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi was Yingzong's former name.

sentences.zh: 琦等遂力贊之，議乃定。

translations.literal: Qi and the others then strongly supported him and the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and the others then strongly supported him and the decision was settled.

sentences.zh: 英宗居濮王喪，議起知宗正。

translations.literal: Yingzong was in mourning for Prince Pu; it was proposed to appoint him director of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong was in mourning for Prince Pu; it was proposed to appoint him director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「事若行，不可中止。

translations.literal: Qi said: "If this matter proceeds it cannot be halted midway.
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "If this matter proceeds it cannot be halted midway.

sentences.zh: 陛下斷自不疑，乞內中批出。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must decide without doubt—I beg that an order be issued from within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must decide without doubt—I beg that an order be issued from within the palace."

sentences.zh: 」帝意不欲宮人知，曰：「只中書行足矣。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish palace women to know and said: "Let the Secretariat handle it—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish palace women to know and said, "Let the Secretariat handle it—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 」命下，英宗固辭。

translations.literal: When the order was issued Yingzong firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the order was issued Yingzong firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝復問琦，琦對曰：「陛下既知其賢而選之，今不敢遽當，蓋器識遠大，所以為賢也。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked Qi; Qi answered: "Your Majesty already knew his worth and chose him; that he now dares not accept at once is precisely because his capacity and vision are far-reaching—that is why he is worthy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked Qi; Qi answered, "Your Majesty already knew his worth and chose him; that he now dares not accept at once is precisely because his capacity and vision are far-reaching—that is why he is worthy."

sentences.zh: 願固起之。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will firmly press him to take office."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will firmly press him to take office."

sentences.zh: 」英宗既終喪，猶堅臥不起。

translations.literal: After Yingzong had completed his mourning he still lay abed and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong had completed his mourning he still lay abed and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 琦言：「宗正之命初出，外人皆知必為皇子，不若遂正其名。

translations.literal: Qi said: "When the command from the Directorate of Imperial Clans was first issued, everyone outside already knew he would surely be made imperial prince—it would be better to go ahead and formally establish his title.
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "When the order from the Directorate of Imperial Clans first went out, everyone outside the palace already knew he would be made imperial prince. It would be better to go ahead and formally establish his title.

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔立為皇子。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued establishing him as imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued establishing him as imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 明年，英宗嗣位，以琦為仁宗山陵使，加門下侍郎，進封衛國公。

translations.literal: The next year, when Yingzong succeeded to the throne, Qi was made overseer of Emperor Renzong's mausoleum, promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and advanced in rank to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Yingzong succeeded to the throne, Qi was appointed overseer of Emperor Renzong's mausoleum, promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 琦既輔立英宗，門人親客，或從容語及定策事，琦必正色曰：「此仁宗聖德神斷，為天下計，皇太后內助之力，臣子何與焉。

translations.literal: After Qi had helped establish Yingzong as heir, among his students and close associates some would casually speak of the succession decision; Qi always replied with a stern countenance: "This was Emperor Renzong's sagely virtue and divine resolve, undertaken for the sake of the realm—the Empress Dowager's support from within—what part did we subjects have in it?
translations.idiomatic: After Qi had helped establish Yingzong as heir, some among his students and close associates would casually mention the succession decision. Qi always replied sternly, "This was Emperor Renzong's sagely virtue and divine resolve, undertaken for the sake of the realm, with the Empress Dowager's support from within. What part did we subjects have in it?

sentences.zh: 」英宗暴得疾，太后垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: Yingzong suddenly fell ill, and the Empress Dowager held court from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong suddenly fell ill, and the Empress Dowager held court from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 帝疾甚，舉措或改常度，遇宦官尤少恩，左右多不悅者，乃共為讒間，兩宮遂成隙。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness was severe; his conduct sometimes departed from his usual manner, and he showed eunuchs especially little favor. Many of those around him were displeased, and together they wove slander to drive a wedge between the two palaces, and a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness was severe. His conduct sometimes departed from his usual manner, and he showed eunuchs especially little favor. Many of those around him were displeased and together wove slander to drive a wedge between the two palaces, and a rift arose between emperor and empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 琦與歐陽修奏事簾前，太后嗚咽流涕，具道所以，琦曰：「此病固爾，病已，必不然。

translations.literal: Qi and Ouyang Xiu reported affairs before the curtain. The Empress Dowager sobbed and wept, fully explaining the reasons. Qi said: "This illness is indeed like that; once the illness passes, it will surely not be so.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Ouyang Xiu reported affairs before the curtain. The Empress Dowager sobbed and wept, fully explaining what had happened. Qi said, "This illness is indeed like that. Once the illness passes, it will surely not be so.

sentences.zh: 子疾，母可不容之乎？

translations.literal: When a son is ill, can a mother fail to tolerate him?
translations.idiomatic: When a son is ill, can a mother fail to tolerate him?

sentences.zh: 」修亦委曲進言，太后意稍和，久之而罷。

translations.literal: Xiu also tactfully advanced his views, and the Empress Dowager's mood gradually softened; after a long while the session ended.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu also spoke tactfully, and the Empress Dowager's mood gradually softened. After a long while the audience ended.

sentences.zh: 後數日，琦獨見上，上曰：「太后待我無恩。

translations.literal: Several days later Qi had a private audience with the emperor. The emperor said: "The Empress Dowager shows me no kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Qi had a private audience with the emperor. The emperor said, "The Empress Dowager shows me no kindness.

sentences.zh: 」琦對曰：「自古聖帝明王，不為少矣。

translations.literal: Qi replied: "From antiquity there have been no few sage emperors and enlightened kings.
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "From antiquity there have been no few sage emperors and enlightened kings.

sentences.zh: 然獨稱舜為大孝，豈其餘盡不孝耶？

translations.literal: Yet only Shun is called supremely filial—are all the rest utterly unfilial?
translations.idiomatic: Yet only Shun is called supremely filial. Are all the rest utterly unfilial?

sentences.zh: 父母慈愛而子孝，此常事不足道；

translations.literal: When parents are loving and the child is filial, that is ordinary and not worth mentioning;
translations.idiomatic: When parents are loving and the child is filial, that is ordinary and not worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 惟父母不慈，而子不失孝，乃為可稱。

translations.literal: Only when parents are not loving yet the child does not cease to be filial is it truly praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Only when parents are not loving yet the child does not cease to be filial is it truly praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 但恐陛下事之未至爾，父母豈有不慈者哉。

translations.literal: I only fear that Your Majesty's service has not yet reached that standard—for how could parents ever fail to be loving?
translations.idiomatic: I only fear that Your Majesty's service has not yet reached that standard, for how could parents ever fail to be loving?

sentences.zh: 」帝大感悟。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply moved to insight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and came to a new understanding.

sentences.zh: 及疾愈，琦請乘輿因禱雨具素服以出，人情乃安。

translations.literal: When the illness had passed, Qi requested that the imperial carriage go out for rain-prayers dressed in plain white mourning garb, and public sentiment was then reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness had passed, Qi requested that the emperor go out in the imperial carriage for rain-prayers dressed in plain white mourning garb, and public sentiment was then reassured.

sentences.zh: 太后還政，拜琦右僕射，封魏國公。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager returned authority to the throne, Qi was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager returned authority to the throne, Qi was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇大順，琦議停歲賜，絕和市，遣使問罪。

translations.literal: When the Western Xia raided Dashun, Qi proposed halting the annual stipend, cutting off border trade, and sending envoys to demand accountability.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Xia raided Dashun, Qi proposed halting the annual stipend, cutting off border trade, and sending envoys to demand accountability.

sentences.zh: 樞密使文彥博難之，或舉寶元、康定事，琦曰：「諒祚，狂童也，非有元昊智計，而邊備過當時遠甚。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Wen Yanbo objected, citing precedents from the Baoyuan and Kangding eras. Qi said: "Liangzuo is a reckless youth—he lacks Yuan Hao's cunning—and our frontier defenses today far exceed those of that time.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Wen Yanbo objected, citing precedents from the Baoyuan and Kangding eras. Qi said, "Liangzuo is a reckless youth. He lacks Yuan Hao's cunning, and our frontier defenses today far exceed those of that time.

sentences.zh: 亟詰之，必服。

translations.literal: Press him hard at once and he is sure to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Press him hard at once and he is sure to submit.

sentences.zh: 」既而諒祚上表謝，帝顧琦曰：「一如所料。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Liangzuo submitted a memorial of apology. The emperor turned to Qi and said: "Just as you predicted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liangzuo submitted a memorial of apology. The emperor turned to Qi and said, "Just as you predicted.

sentences.zh: 」帝寢疾，琦入問起居，言曰：「陛下久不視朝，願早建儲，以安社稷。

translations.literal: The emperor took to his bed with illness. Qi entered to inquire after his health and said: "Your Majesty has long ceased to hold court—I hope you will soon establish an heir to secure the state and altars.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took to his bed with illness. Qi entered to inquire after his health and said, "Your Majesty has long ceased to hold court. I hope you will soon establish an heir to secure the state and altars.

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之，即召學士草制，立潁王。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent, and immediately summoned academicians to draft the edict establishing the Prince of Ying as heir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded assent and immediately summoned academicians to draft the edict establishing the Prince of Ying as heir.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，拜司空兼侍中，為英宗山陵使。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Qi was appointed Grand Minister of Works and concurrently Palace Attendant, and made overseer of Emperor Yingzong's mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Qi was appointed Grand Minister of Works and concurrently Palace Attendant, and made overseer of Emperor Yingzong's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 琦執政三世，或病其專。

translations.literal: Qi had held power through three reigns, and some faulted him for being domineering.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had held power through three reigns, and some faulted him for being domineering.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王陶劾琦不赴文德殿押班為跋扈。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao impeached Qi for failing to attend the escort formation at the Wende Hall, calling it arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao impeached Qi for failing to attend the escort formation at the Wende Hall, calling it arrogance.

sentences.zh: 琦請去，帝為黜陶。

translations.literal: Qi requested to leave office; the emperor dismissed Tao on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Qi requested to leave office, and the emperor dismissed Tao on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 永厚陵復土，琦不復入中書，堅辭位。

translations.literal: When the earth was replaced over Yonghou Mausoleum, Qi did not return to the Secretariat and firmly declined the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the earth was replaced over Yonghou Mausoleum, Qi did not return to the Secretariat and firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 除鎮安武勝軍節度使、司徒兼侍中、判相州。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of the Zhen'an and Wusheng Armies, Grand Tutor and concurrently Palace Attendant, with concurrent service as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Zhen'an and Wusheng Armies, Grand Tutor and concurrently Palace Attendant, with concurrent service as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝泣曰：「侍中必欲去，今日已降制矣。

translations.literal: On entering for audience the emperor wept and said: "Attendant-in-waiting, you are determined to leave—today the appointment has already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: On entering for audience the emperor wept and said, "Attendant-in-waiting, you are determined to leave. Today the appointment has already been issued.

sentences.zh: 」賜興道坊宅一區，擢其子忠彥秘閣校理。

translations.literal: He was granted one residence in Xingdao Ward, and his son Zhongyan was promoted to collator in the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one residence in Xingdao Ward, and his son Zhongyan was promoted to collator in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 琦辭兩鎮，乃但領淮南。

translations.literal: Qi declined both military commissions and accepted only charge of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi declined both military commissions and accepted only charge of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 會种諤擅取綏州，西邊俶擾，改判永興軍，經略陝西。

translations.literal: Just then Zhong E seized Suizhou on his own authority and the western frontier was suddenly in turmoil; Qi was reassigned to Yongxing Army and made grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zhong E seized Suizhou on his own authority and the western frontier was suddenly in turmoil. Qi was reassigned to Yongxing Army and made grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 琦言：「邊臣肆意妄作，棄約基亂，願召二府亟決之。

translations.literal: Qi said: "Frontier officials have acted recklessly on their own, abandoning treaties and laying groundwork for chaos—I hope the two palaces can be summoned at once to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "Frontier officials have acted recklessly on their own, abandoning treaties and laying groundwork for chaos. I hope the two palaces can be summoned at once to decide.

sentences.zh: 」琦入辭，曾公亮等方奏事，乞與琦同議。

translations.literal: When Qi entered to take leave of office, Zeng Gongliang and others were just reporting affairs and requested to deliberate together with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi entered to take leave of office, Zeng Gongliang and others were just reporting affairs and requested to deliberate together with Qi.

sentences.zh: 帝召之，琦曰：「臣前日備員政府，所當共議。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him. Qi said: "The other day I was still a member of the government and ought to have deliberated together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him. Qi said, "The other day I was still a member of the government and ought to have deliberated together.

sentences.zh: 今日，藩臣也，不敢預聞。

translations.literal: Today I am a frontier commissioner and dare not intrude on such matters.
translations.idiomatic: Today I am a frontier commissioner and dare not intrude on such matters.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「王陶指臣為跋扈，今陛下乃舉陝西兵柄授臣，復有劾臣如陶者，則臣赤族矣。

translations.literal: He added: "Wang Tao called me domineering; now Your Majesty invests me with military authority over Shaanxi—if there are again impeachments like Tao's, then my whole clan will be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Wang Tao called me domineering. Now Your Majesty invests me with military authority over Shaanxi. If there are again impeachments like Tao's, then my whole clan will be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「侍中猶未知朕意邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Attendant-in-waiting, do you still not know my intent?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Attendant-in-waiting, do you still not know my intent?

sentences.zh: 」琦初言綏州不當取，已而夏人誘殺楊定，琦復言：「賊既如此，綏今不可棄」。

translations.literal: Qi had at first said Suizhou should not be taken; later, when the Western Xia lured and killed Yang Ding, Qi said again: "Since the enemy has acted thus, Suizhou cannot now be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Qi had at first said Suizhou should not be taken. Later, when the Western Xia lured and killed Yang Ding, Qi said again, "Since the enemy has acted thus, Suizhou cannot now be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 樞密院以初議詰之，琦具論其故，卒存之。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs questioned him on his original view; Qi fully explained the reasons, and Suizhou was finally retained.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs questioned him on his original view. Qi fully explained the reasons, and Suizhou was finally retained.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年七月，復請相州以歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Xining, he again requested to return to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Xining, he again requested to return to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 河北地震、河決，徒判大名府，充安撫使，得便宜從事。

translations.literal: When Hebei suffered an earthquake and the Yellow River burst its banks, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Daming Prefecture and pacification commissioner, with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei suffered an earthquake and the Yellow River burst its banks, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Daming Prefecture and pacification commissioner, with authority to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 王安石用事，出常平使者散青苗錢。

translations.literal: With Wang Anshi in power, Granary emissaries were dispatched to distribute Green Sprouts loans.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Anshi in power, Granary emissaries were dispatched to distribute Green Sprouts loans.

sentences.zh: 琦亟言之。

translations.literal: Qi urgently memorialized on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Qi urgently memorialized on the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝袖其疏以示宰臣，曰：「琦真忠臣，雖在外，不忘王室。

translations.literal: The emperor tucked the memorial in his sleeve and showed it to the chief ministers, saying: "Qi is a true loyal minister—though outside the capital, he has not forgotten the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tucked the memorial in his sleeve and showed it to the chief ministers, saying, "Qi is a true loyal minister. Though outside the capital, he has not forgotten the royal house.

sentences.zh: 朕始謂可以利民，今乃害民如此。

translations.literal: I at first thought it could benefit the people; now it harms them to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: I at first thought it could benefit the people. Now it harms them to this extent.

sentences.zh: 且坊郭安得青苗，而亦強與之乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, how can urban districts receive Green Sprouts loans—and yet they are forced to accept them?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, how can urban districts receive Green Sprouts loans, and yet they are forced to accept them?

sentences.zh: 」安石勃然進曰：「苟從其欲，雖坊郭何害。

translations.literal: Anshi stepped forward in anger and said: "If we follow their wishes, what harm even to urban districts?
translations.idiomatic: Anshi stepped forward in anger and said, "If we follow their wishes, what harm even to urban districts?

sentences.zh: 」明日，稱疾不出。

translations.literal: The next day he claimed illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he claimed illness and did not attend court.

sentences.zh: 當是時，新法幾罷，安石復出，持前議益堅。

translations.literal: At that time the New Policies were nearly abolished; Anshi returned to office and held to his earlier views all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the New Policies were nearly abolished. Anshi returned to office and held to his earlier views all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 琦又懇奏，安石下之條例司，令其屬疏駁，刊石頒天下。

translations.literal: Qi again submitted earnest memorials; Anshi referred them to the Regulatory Bureau and had subordinates write refutations, which were carved in stone and issued throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Qi again submitted earnest memorials. Anshi referred them to the Regulatory Bureau and had subordinates write refutations, which were carved in stone and issued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 琦申辨愈切，不克從。

translations.literal: Qi's rebuttals grew ever more urgent, but he could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's rebuttals grew ever more urgent, but he could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 於是請解四路安撫使，止領一路，安石欲沮琦，即從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested to be relieved of the four-way pacification commission and to retain only one circuit; Anshi, wishing to frustrate Qi, assented at once.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he requested to be relieved of the four-way pacification commission and to retain only one circuit. Anshi, wishing to frustrate Qi, assented at once.

sentences.zh: 六年，還判相州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he returned to serve as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned to serve as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹來求代北地，帝手詔訪琦，琦奏言：

translations.literal: The Khitan came seeking territory north of Dai; the emperor sent a personal edict seeking Qi's views, and Qi memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan came seeking territory north of Dai. The emperor sent a personal edict seeking Qi's views, and Qi memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「臣觀近年以來，朝廷舉事，似不以大敵為恤。

translations.literal: In my view, in recent years when the court undertakes measures, it seems not to concern itself with the great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, in recent years when the court undertakes measures, it seems not to concern itself with the great enemy.

sentences.zh: 彼見形生疑，必謂我有圖復燕南意，故引先發制人之說，造為釁端。

translations.literal: Seeing these signs they grow suspicious and must believe we intend to recover Yan South; so they invoke the doctrine of striking first, and manufacture pretexts for conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing these signs they grow suspicious and must believe we intend to recover Yan South. So they invoke the doctrine of striking first and manufacture pretexts for conflict.

sentences.zh: 所以致疑，其事有七：高麗臣屬北方，久絕朝貢，乃因商舶誘之使來，契丹知之，必謂將以圖我。

translations.literal: The matters that have aroused suspicion are seven in number: Goryeo, though subject to the north, had long ceased tribute; yet through merchant ships we induced them to come—when the Khitan learned of this they surely believed we intended to move against them.
translations.idiomatic: The matters that have aroused suspicion are seven in number. Goryeo, though subject to the north, had long ceased tribute, yet through merchant ships we induced them to come. When the Khitan learned of this they surely believed we intended to move against them.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: The first.
translations.idiomatic: The first.

sentences.zh: 強取吐蕃之地以建熙河，契丹聞之，必謂行將及我。

translations.literal: Forcibly seizing Tibetan territory to establish Xihé Circuit—when the Khitan heard of this they surely believed it would soon reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Forcibly seizing Tibetan territory to establish Xihé Circuit—when the Khitan heard of this they surely believed it would soon reach them.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: The second.
translations.idiomatic: The second.

sentences.zh: 遍植榆柳于西山，冀其成長以制蕃騎。

translations.literal: Planting elms and willows widely on the Western Hills, hoping that when they grew they would check nomadic cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Planting elms and willows widely on the Western Hills, hoping that when they grew they would check nomadic cavalry.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: The third.
translations.idiomatic: The third.

sentences.zh: 創團保甲。

translations.literal: Establishing the tuanbao militia system.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing the tuanbao militia system.

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: The fourth.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth.

sentences.zh: 諸州築城鑿池。

translations.literal: Building walls and digging moats in the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Building walls and digging moats in the various prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: The fifth.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth.

sentences.zh: 置都作院，頒弓刀新式，大作戰車。

translations.literal: Establishing the Directorate of Works, issuing new patterns for bows and blades, and building battle chariots on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing the Directorate of Works, issuing new patterns for bows and blades, and building battle chariots on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 六也。

translations.literal: The sixth.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth.

sentences.zh: 置河北三十七將。

translations.literal: Establishing thirty-seven garrison commands in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing thirty-seven garrison commands in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 七也。

translations.literal: The seventh.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh.

sentences.zh: 契丹素為敵國，因事起疑，不得不然。

translations.literal: The Khitan have long been an enemy state; given these events it is only natural that suspicion should arise.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan have long been an enemy state. Given these events it is only natural that suspicion should arise.

sentences.zh: 臣昔年論青苗錢事，言者輒肆厚誣，非陛下之明，幾及大戮。

translations.literal: When I spoke years ago on Green Sprouts loans, critics at once heaped gross slander upon me; but for Your Majesty's clear judgment I would nearly have suffered capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When I spoke years ago on Green Sprouts loans, critics at once heaped gross slander upon me. But for Your Majesty's clear judgment I would nearly have suffered capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 自此，聞新法日下，不敢復言。

translations.literal: Since then, hearing new laws issued daily, I have not dared speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Since then, hearing new laws issued daily, I have not dared speak again.

sentences.zh: 今親被詔問，事系安危，言及而隱，死有餘罪。

translations.literal: Now personally questioned by imperial edict, with the matter touching on safety and peril—to speak yet conceal would leave me guilty even in death.
translations.idiomatic: Now personally questioned by imperial edict, with the matter touching on safety and peril, to speak yet conceal would leave me guilty even in death.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗竊計，始為陛下謀者，必曰治國之本，當先聚財積穀，募兵於民，則可以鞭笞四夷。

translations.literal: I have privately reflected that those who first advised Your Majesty must have said: the foundation of governing the state is first to amass wealth and store grain and levy troops from the people—then one can whip the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: I have privately reflected that those who first advised Your Majesty must have said that the foundation of governing the state is first to amass wealth and store grain and levy troops from the people, and then one can whip the four barbarians.

sentences.zh: 故散青苗錢，使民出利；

translations.literal: Hence Green Sprouts loans were distributed, making the people pay interest;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Green Sprouts loans were distributed, making the people pay interest.

sentences.zh: 為免役之法，次第取錢；

translations.literal: The exemption-from-corvée law was instituted, collecting funds step by step;
translations.idiomatic: The exemption-from-corvée law was instituted, collecting funds step by step.

sentences.zh: 迨置市易務，而小商細民，無所措手。

translations.literal: Then the Market Exchange Office was established, and petty merchants and common folk had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Market Exchange Office was established, and petty merchants and common folk had nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 新制日下，更改無常，官吏茫然，不能詳記，監司督責，以刻為明。

translations.literal: New regulations issue daily, changed without cease; officials are bewildered and cannot keep detailed track; supervisory commissioners press for accountability, taking harshness for clarity.
translations.idiomatic: New regulations issue daily and are changed without cease. Officials are bewildered and cannot keep detailed track. Supervisory commissioners press for accountability, taking harshness for clarity.

sentences.zh: 今農怨於甽畝，商歎于道路，長吏不安其職，陛下不盡知也。

translations.literal: Now farmers grumble in the fields, merchants sigh on the roads, chief officials are uneasy in their posts—Your Majesty does not fully know this.
translations.idiomatic: Now farmers grumble in the fields, merchants sigh on the roads, and chief officials are uneasy in their posts. Your Majesty does not fully know this.

sentences.zh: 夫欲攘斥四夷，以興太平，而先使邦本困搖，眾心離怨，此則為陛下始謀者大誤也。

translations.literal: To wish to repel the four barbarians and bring forth great peace, yet first to leave the foundation of the state shaken and hearts alienated in resentment—this is a grave error by those who first counseled Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: To wish to repel the four barbarians and bring forth great peace, yet first to leave the foundation of the state shaken and hearts alienated in resentment—this is a grave error by those who first counseled Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣今為陛下計，謂宜遣使報聘，具言向來興作，乃修備之常，豈有他意；

translations.literal: For Your Majesty I now propose: envoys should be sent on a return visit, fully explaining that recent undertakings are routine defense preparations, with no other intent;
translations.idiomatic: For Your Majesty I now propose that envoys should be sent on a return visit, fully explaining that recent undertakings are routine defense preparations, with no other intent.

sentences.zh: 疆土素定，悉如舊境，不可持此造端，以隳累世之好。

translations.literal: boundaries have long been fixed and should remain as before—this must not be used to create trouble and destroy goodwill accumulated over generations.
translations.idiomatic: Boundaries have long been fixed and should remain as before. This must not be used to create trouble and destroy goodwill accumulated over generations.

sentences.zh: 以可疑之形，如將官之類，因而罷去。

translations.literal: Where forms look suspicious, such as garrison officers, abolish them on that pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Where forms look suspicious, such as garrison officers, abolish them on that pretext.

sentences.zh: 益養民愛力，選賢任能，疏遠奸諛，進用忠鯁，使天下悅服，邊備日充。

translations.literal: Nurture the people and spare their strength all the more; select the worthy and employ the capable; keep sycophants at a distance and advance the loyal and forthright—so that all under Heaven are pleased and frontier defenses grow daily stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Nurture the people and spare their strength all the more. Select the worthy and employ the capable, keep sycophants at a distance and advance the loyal and forthright, so that all under Heaven are pleased and frontier defenses grow daily stronger.

sentences.zh: 若其果自敗盟，則可一振威武，恢復故疆，攄累朝之宿憤矣。」

translations.literal: If they truly break the alliance of their own accord, then in one stroke we can raise our martial majesty, recover our former territory, and vent the accumulated fury of successive dynasties."
translations.idiomatic: If they truly break the alliance of their own accord, then in one stroke we can raise our martial majesty, recover our former territory, and vent the accumulated fury of successive dynasties."

sentences.zh: 疏上，會安石再入相，悉以所爭地與契丹，東西七百里，論者惜之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Anshi had just returned as chief minister; all the disputed territory was ceded to the Khitan—seven hundred li east to west—and commentators lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Anshi had just returned as chief minister. All the disputed territory was ceded to the Khitan—seven hundred li east to west—and commentators lamented it.

sentences.zh: 八年，換節永興軍，再任，未拜而薨，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred with a new commission to Yongxing Army for a second term; before he could assume the post he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred with a new commission to Yongxing Army for a second term. Before he could assume the post he died, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 前一夕，大星隕於治所，櫪馬皆驚。

translations.literal: On the eve before, a great star fell at his place of administration and the stable horses were all startled.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve before, a great star fell at his place of administration and the stable horses were all startled.

sentences.zh: 帝發哀苑中，哭之慟。

translations.literal: The emperor came forth from the palace mourning grounds and wept bitterly for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came forth from the palace mourning grounds and wept bitterly for him.

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，賜銀三千兩，絹三千匹，發兩河卒為治塚，篆其碑曰「兩朝顧命定策元勳」。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days; three thousand taels of silver and three thousand bolts of silk were granted; troops from the two Hebei circuits were mobilized to build his tomb, and his stele was inscribed: "Founding Merit Minister of Succession Entrusted by Two Reigns."
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days. Three thousand taels of silver and three thousand bolts of silk were granted. Troops from the two Hebei circuits were mobilized to build his tomb, and his stele was inscribed: "Founding Merit Minister of Succession Entrusted by Two Reigns."

sentences.zh: 贈尚書令，諡曰「忠獻」，配享英宗廟庭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Director of the Department of State Affairs, given the posthumous name "Loyal and Generous," and granted shared sacrifice in Emperor Yingzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Director of the Department of State Affairs, given the posthumous name "Loyal and Generous," and granted shared sacrifice in Emperor Yingzong's temple court.

sentences.zh: 常令其子若孫一人官於相，以護丘墓。

translations.literal: It was decreed that one of his sons or grandsons should always hold office in Xiang to guard his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: It was decreed that one of his sons or grandsons should always hold office in Xiang to guard his tomb.

sentences.zh: 故事，三省長官，惟尚書令為尤重，贈者必兼他官。

translations.literal: By precedent, among the chief officers of the Three Departments, only the Director of the Department of State Affairs was especially exalted; those posthumously granted it must also hold another office.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, among the chief officers of the Three Departments, only the Director of the Department of State Affairs was especially exalted. Those posthumously granted it must also hold another office.

sentences.zh: 至琦，乃單贈。

translations.literal: In Qi's case alone was it granted by itself.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi's case alone was it granted by itself.

sentences.zh: 後又詔，雖當追策，不復更加師保，蓋貴之也。

translations.literal: Later an edict further ruled that though posthumous honors might be added, no further Grand Tutor or Grand Preceptor titles would be added—such was the mark of esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict further ruled that though posthumous honors might be added, no further Grand Tutor or Grand Preceptor titles would be added—such was the mark of esteem.

sentences.zh: 琦蚤有盛名，識量英偉，臨事喜慍不見於色，論者以重厚比周勃，政事比姚崇。

translations.literal: Qi had long enjoyed great renown; his discernment and stature were heroic and imposing. In affairs joy and anger never showed on his face. Commentators compared his weight and steadiness to Zhou Bo and his statecraft to Yao Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had long enjoyed great renown. His discernment and stature were heroic and imposing, and in affairs joy and anger never showed on his face. Commentators compared his weight and steadiness to Zhou Bo and his statecraft to Yao Chong.

sentences.zh: 其為學士臨邊，年甫三十，天下已稱為韓公。

translations.literal: When he served as academician on the frontier, he was barely thirty, yet the realm already called him Lord Han.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as an academician on the frontier, he was barely thirty, yet all under Heaven already called him Lord Han.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐、治平間，再決大策，以安社稷。

translations.literal: Between the Jiayou and Zhiping eras, he twice decided great policies to secure the state and altars.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jiayou and Zhiping reigns, he twice made critical decisions that secured the realm.

sentences.zh: 當是時，朝廷多故，琦處危疑之際，知無不為。

translations.literal: At that time the court had many troubles; Qi faced moments of peril and doubt, and whatever he knew to do, he did.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court faced one crisis after another; Qi stood at moments of peril and doubt and left nothing undone that he knew how to do.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「公所為誠善，萬一蹉跌，豈惟身不自保，恐家無處所。

translations.literal: Someone admonished him, saying: "What you do is truly good, but if you stumble even once, not only might you fail to preserve yourself—I fear your family would have nowhere to go."
translations.idiomatic: Someone remonstrated with him: "What you do is truly good, but if you stumble even once, you may not save yourself—and your family may have nowhere to turn."

sentences.zh: 」琦歎曰：「是何言也。

translations.literal: Qi sighed and said: "What talk is this?
translations.idiomatic: Qi sighed and said: "What sort of talk is that?"

sentences.zh: 今臣盡力事君，死生以之。

translations.literal: Now I exert all my strength in serving the ruler; life and death follow from that.
translations.idiomatic: Now I devote myself utterly to serving my sovereign; my life and death follow from that.

sentences.zh: 至於成敗，天也，豈可豫憂其不濟，遂輟不為哉。

translations.literal: As for success or failure, that is Heaven's doing—how can one worry in advance that it will not succeed and so stop doing what should be done?
translations.idiomatic: As for success or failure, that is Heaven's affair. How can one worry in advance that things will fail, and on that account stop doing what must be done?

sentences.zh: 」聞者愧服。

translations.literal: Those who heard were ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were shamed into agreement.

sentences.zh: 在魏都久，遼使每過，移牒必書名，曰：「以韓公在此故也。

translations.literal: He stayed long at the Wei capital; whenever Liao envoys passed through, their written communications always named him, saying: "Because Lord Han is here.
translations.idiomatic: During his long tenure at the capital of Wei, Liao envoys passing through always named him in their official messages, explaining: "Because Lord Han is here."

sentences.zh: 」忠彥使遼，遼主問知其貌類父，即命工圖之，其見重於外國也如此。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan served as envoy to Liao, the Liao ruler inquired and learned that his appearance resembled his father's; he immediately ordered artisans to paint his portrait. Thus was he esteemed in foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyan served as envoy to Liao, the Liao ruler learned that he resembled his father in appearance and immediately ordered artisans to paint his portrait. Such was the esteem in which the family was held abroad.

sentences.zh: 琦天資樸忠，折節下士，無賤貴，禮之如一。

translations.literal: Qi's inborn nature was plain and loyal; he lowered himself to treat scholars, without regard to humble or noble, treating all with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was plainspoken and loyal by nature. He humbled himself before men of talent, showing the same courtesy to the lowly and the high alike.

sentences.zh: 尤以獎拔人才為急，儻公論所與，雖意所不悅，亦收用之，故得人為多。

translations.literal: He especially made promoting talent urgent; if public opinion endorsed someone, even when he personally disliked the man he still employed him—hence he gathered many able men.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially zealous in advancing talent: if public opinion favored a man, Qi would employ him even when he personally disliked him. Thus he gathered more capable men than most.

sentences.zh: 選飭群司，皆使奉法循理。

translations.literal: In selecting and disciplining the various offices, he made all adhere to law and follow principle.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting and disciplining officials, he required all to obey the law and follow proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 其所建請，第顧義所在，無適莫心。

translations.literal: In his proposals and petitions, he looked only to where righteousness lay, with no partial or distant heart.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorials he cared only where duty lay, without favoritism toward allies or hostility toward foes.

sentences.zh: 在相位時，王安石有盛名，或以為可用，琦獨不然之。

translations.literal: When he held the chancellorship, Wang Anshi had great fame; some thought him usable, but Qi alone dissented.
translations.idiomatic: While Qi was chancellor, Wang Anshi enjoyed great renown; some considered him a suitable appointee, but Qi alone disagreed.

sentences.zh: 及守相，陛辭，神宗曰：「卿去，誰可屬國者，王安石何如？

translations.literal: When he was prefect of a circuit and took leave at audience, Emperor Shenzong said: "When you go, who can be entrusted with the state? What of Wang Anshi?
translations.idiomatic: When he left the capital to serve as a circuit prefect and took formal leave, Emperor Shenzong asked: "After you go, whom can I entrust with the state? What of Wang Anshi?"

sentences.zh: 」琦曰：「安石為翰林學士則有餘，處輔弼之地則不可。

translations.literal: Qi said: "Anshi as Hanlin academician would be more than adequate; in a position as chief counselor he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied: "Anshi would be more than adequate as a Hanlin academician, but he should not be placed among the chief counselors."

sentences.zh: 」上不答。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not answer.

sentences.zh: 其鎮大名也，魏人為立生祠。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned Daming, the people of Wei erected a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was posted to Daming, the people of Wei built a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 相人愛之如父母，有鬥訟，傳相勸止，曰：「勿撓吾侍中也。

translations.literal: The people of Xiangzhou loved him as they would parents; when there were quarrels and lawsuits, word passed from one to another urging restraint, saying: "Do not trouble our Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved him as they would their own parents. When quarrels arose, neighbors urged one another to stop, saying: "Don't trouble our Palace Attendant."

sentences.zh: 」與富弼齊名，號稱賢相，人謂之「富韓」云。

translations.literal: He ranked with Fu Bi in fame; they were called worthy chancellors, and people spoke of them as "Fu and Han."
translations.idiomatic: He stood equal in fame with Fu Bi; together they were hailed as worthy chancellors, and people called them "Fu and Han."

sentences.zh: 徽宗追論琦定策勳，贈魏郡王。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong, reviewing Qi's merit in settling the succession policy, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong, reviewing Qi's merit in settling the succession crisis, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子五人：忠彥、端彥、純彥、粹彥、嘉彥。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Zhongyan, Duanyan, Chunyan, Cuiyan, and Jiayan.
