translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Zhongyan, Duanyan, Chunyan, Cuiyan, and Jiayan.

sentences.zh: 端彥右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: Duanyan was Right Assistant Master of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Duanyan held the rank of Right Assistant Master of the Household.

sentences.zh: 純彥官至徽猷閣直學士。

translations.literal: Chunyan rose to Direct Academician of the Hall of Glorious Attainments.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyan rose to the post of Direct Academician of the Hall of Glorious Attainments.

sentences.zh: 粹彥為吏部侍郎，終龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: Cuiyan served as Vice Minister of Personnel and ended as Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Cuiyan served as Vice Minister of Personnel and died as Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉彥尚神宗女齊國公主，拜駙馬都尉，終瀛海軍承宣使。

translations.literal: Jiayan married Emperor Shenzong's daughter, the Princess of Qi State, was appointed Commandant-consort of the Princess, and ended as Commissioner of the Yinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayan married Emperor Shenzong's daughter, the Princess of Qi, was appointed Commandant of the Princess's Household, and died as Commissioner of the Yinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 子 忠彥

translations.literal: Son: Zhongyan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zhongyan

sentences.zh: 忠彥，字師樸，少以父任，為將作監簿，復舉進士。

translations.literal: Zhongyan, styled Shipu, in youth entered through his father's privilege as Clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan, styled Shipu, began his career through his father's privilege as Clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 琦罷政，忠彥以秘書丞召試館職，除校理、同知太常禮院，為開封府判官、三司鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: When Qi left the chancellorship, Zhongyan was summoned as Secretary of the Secretariat to test for a palace post, was appointed Collator and Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Ceremonies, and served as investigating officer of Kaifeng prefecture and fiscal judge of the Salt and Iron Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi left office, Zhongyan was summoned from his post as Secretary of the Secretariat to qualify for a palace appointment. He was made Collator and Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Ceremonies, then served as investigating officer of Kaifeng and fiscal judge of the Salt and Iron Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出通判永寧軍，召還，為戶部判官。

translations.literal: He went out as deputy prefect of Yongning Army, was recalled, and served as fiscal judge of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as deputy prefect of Yongning Army, then recalled to serve as fiscal judge of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 使還。

translations.literal: He returned from his mission.
translations.idiomatic: He returned from his diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 時官制行，章惇為門下侍郎，奏：「給事中，東省屬官，封駁宜先稟而後上。

translations.literal: At that time the new bureaucracy was implemented; Zhang Dun, as Vice Director of the Chancellery, memorialized: "The Supervisor of Remonstrance is an official subordinate to the Eastern Secretariat; review and rejection of edicts should first be reported upward and only then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the new bureaucracy was taking effect. Zhang Dun, serving as Vice Director of the Chancellery, memorialized: "The Supervisor of Remonstrance is a subordinate of the Eastern Secretariat; edicts proposed for review should first be reported to superiors before submission."

sentences.zh: 」忠彥奏：「朝廷之事，執政之所行也。

translations.literal: Zhongyan memorialized: "Affairs of the court are what the chief administrators carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan countered: "Court affairs are the province of the chief administrators."

sentences.zh: 事當封駁，則與執政固已異矣，尚何稟議之有。

translations.literal: When something should be reviewed and rejected, one is already at odds with the administrators—what need is there to report and consult?
translations.idiomatic: When an edict warrants rejection, one is already at odds with the administrators—why report and consult with them first?

sentences.zh: 」詔從其請。

translations.literal: An edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his position.

sentences.zh: 左僕射王珪為南郊大禮使，事之當下者，自從其所畫旨。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Gui served as Grand Ceremonial Officer for the Southern Suburban Sacrifice; urgent matters were handled on his own written directives.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Gui served as Grand Ceremonial Officer for the Southern Suburban Sacrifice and handled urgent matters on his own written directives.

sentences.zh: 忠彥以官制駁之曰：「今事於南郊者，大禮使既不從中畫旨，處分出一時者，又不從中書奏審。

translations.literal: Zhongyan rejected this on grounds of the bureaucracy, saying: "Now in matters of the Southern Suburban Sacrifice, the Grand Ceremonial Officer neither follows central written directives, nor do expedient decisions go through the Secretariat for review and approval.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan objected on grounds of the new bureaucracy: "For the Southern Suburban Sacrifice, the Grand Ceremonial Officer acts without central directives, and urgent decisions bypass Secretariat review altogether."

sentences.zh: 官制之行，曾未期月，而廟堂自渝之，後將若之何？

translations.literal: The bureaucracy has been in force barely a full month, yet the court itself violates it—what will become of things hereafter?
translations.idiomatic: The new system has been in force barely a month, yet the court is already undermining it—what will become of governance hereafter?

sentences.zh: 」乃詔事無鉅細，必經三省而後行。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered that matters great and small must pass through the Three Departments before implementation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued requiring all matters, great and small, to pass through the Three Departments before taking effect.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部尚書，以樞密直學士知定州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites and served as Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs governing Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites and, as Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, governed Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 進左僕射兼門下侍郎，封儀國公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 而曾布為右相，多不協，言事者助布排忠彥，以觀文殿大學士知大名府。

translations.literal: But Zeng Bu was chief counselor on the right; they often failed to agree. Remonstrators helped Bu drive out Zhongyan, and he was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture governing Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu held the right chancellorship and they often clashed. Critics of policy sided with Bu to drive Zhongyan out, and he was reassigned as Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture to govern Daming.

sentences.zh: 又以欽聖欲復廢后，為忠彥罪，再降太中大夫，懷州居住。

translations.literal: Further, because Empress Dowager Qinsheng wished to restore the deposed empress, this was made Zhongyan's crime; he was demoted again to Grand Master of Palace Affairs and ordered to reside in Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was also charged with Empress Dowager Qinsheng's attempt to restore the deposed empress, demoted again to Grand Master of Palace Affairs, and ordered to live in Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又論忠彥在相位，不應棄湟州，謫崇信軍節度副使，濟州居住。

translations.literal: It was further argued that while in the chancellorship Zhongyan should not have abandoned Huangzhou; he was relegated to Military Vice Commissioner of Chongxin Army and ordered to reside in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was further accused of having wrongly abandoned Huangzhou while chancellor, relegated to Military Vice Commissioner of Chongxin Army, and ordered to live in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 逮復湟、鄯，又謫磁州團練副使。

translations.literal: When Huang and Zuo were recovered, he was demoted again to Vice Commissioner for Training of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang and Zuo were recovered, he was demoted again to Vice Commissioner for Training of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 復太中大夫，遂以宣奉大夫致仕。

translations.literal: His rank of Grand Master of Palace Affairs was restored, and he finally retired with the title of Grand Master for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was restored to Grand Master of Palace Affairs, and he finally retired with the title of Grand Master for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子治，徽宗時，為太僕少卿，出知相州。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, in the Huizong era, served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and went out to govern Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, under Emperor Huizong, served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and was posted to govern Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以疾丐祠，命其子肖胄代之，別有傳。

translations.literal: Illness led him to request a sinecure post; his son Xiaozhou was ordered to replace him; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to request a sinecure; his son Xiaozhou was appointed in his place. He has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：琦相三朝，立二帝，厥功大矣。

translations.literal: In appraisal: Qi served as chancellor through three reigns and established two emperors—his merit was great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Qi served as chancellor through three reigns and helped establish two emperors—his achievement was immense.

sentences.zh: 當治平危疑之際，兩宮幾成嫌隙，琦處之裕如，卒安社稷，人服其量。

translations.literal: At the perilous and uncertain moment of the Zhiping era, the two palaces nearly developed mutual resentment; Qi handled it with ease and finally secured the state and altars—men admired his breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: At the perilous moment of the Zhiping era, when friction nearly opened between the two palaces, Qi handled the crisis with composure and in the end secured the realm. All admired the breadth of his mind.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修稱其「臨大事，決大議，垂紳正笏，不動聲色，措天下于泰山之安，可謂社稷之臣」。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu praised him: "Facing great affairs and deciding great counsels, with sash hanging and tablet straight, without change of voice or countenance, he set the realm on the security of Mount Tai—he may be called a pillar of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu praised him: "In great crises and on great decisions, sash hanging and tablet held straight, he never changed voice or expression, and set the realm on a foundation as firm as Mount Tai—truly a pillar of the state."

sentences.zh: 豈不信哉！

translations.literal: Is this not worthy of belief!
translations.idiomatic: Could this be doubted?

sentences.zh: 忠彥世濟其美，繼登相位，宜矣。

translations.literal: Zhongyan through generations carried on this excellence and in turn ascended the chancellorship—fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan inherited this excellence and in his turn rose to the chancellorship—as was fitting.

sentences.zh: 曾公亮

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang

sentences.zh: 曾公亮，字明仲，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang, styled Mingzhong, was a man of Jinjiang in Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang, styled Mingzhong, was a native of Jinjiang in Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，知會稽縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the top grade and governed Kuaiji county.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Kuaiji County.

sentences.zh: 民田鏡湖旁，每患湖溢。

translations.literal: The people's fields lay beside Mirror Lake, and they were afflicted each year when the lake overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Local fields lay beside Mirror Lake, and each year the people suffered when the lake overflowed.

sentences.zh: 公亮立斗門，泄水入曹娥江，民受其利。

translations.literal: Gongliang built sluice gates, draining water into the Cao'e River, and the people received the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang built sluice gates to drain overflow into the Cao'e River, to the people's great benefit.

sentences.zh: 坐父買田境中，謫監湖州酒。

translations.literal: For his father's buying land within the jurisdiction, he was demoted to supervisor of the Huzhou wine monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had purchased land within his jurisdiction, he was demoted to supervisor of the Huzhou wine monopoly.

sentences.zh: 久之，為國子監直講，改諸王府侍講。

translations.literal: After some time he became Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education and was transferred to Lecturer of the Various Princes' Households.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education, then Lecturer of the Various Princes' Households.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，當用故事試館職，獨獻所為文，授集賢校理、天章閣侍講、修起居注。

translations.literal: When his term ended he should, by precedent, have tested for a palace post; he alone submitted writings he had composed and was appointed Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Lecturer of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, and Compiler of the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he should by precedent have tested for a palace appointment; instead he submitted writings of his own and was appointed Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Lecturer of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, and Compiler of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Reserve Master of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Reserve Master of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and granted the gold seal and purple robe of high office.

sentences.zh: 先是，待制不改服。

translations.literal: Previously, Reserve Masters did not change their dress.
translations.idiomatic: Until then, Reserve Masters had not changed their official dress.

sentences.zh: 仁宗面錫之，曰：「朕自講席賜卿，所以尊寵儒臣也。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong personally bestowed it on him, saying: "I grant this to you from the lecture hall, to honor and favor a Confucian minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong personally bestowed the honor, saying: "I grant this from my own lecture hall, to honor and exalt a Confucian minister."

sentences.zh: 」遂知制誥兼史館修撰，為翰林學士、判三班院。

translations.literal: He then became Drafting Officer for Proclamations concurrent Compiler for the Historiography Hall, and served as Hanlin Academician directing the Three Ranks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Drafting Officer for Proclamations and Compiler for the Historiography Hall, and served as Hanlin Academician directing the Three Ranks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 三班吏叢猥，非賕謝不行，貴遊子弟，多倚勢請謁。

translations.literal: The clerks of the Three Ranks Bureau were disorderly and base; nothing was done without bribes; sons of noble families mostly relied on influence to request favors.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks of the Three Ranks Bureau were a disorderly lot; nothing moved without a bribe, and the sons of powerful families relied on patronage to get their way.

sentences.zh: 公亮掇前後章程，視以從事，吏不能舉手。

translations.literal: Gongliang gathered earlier and later regulations and held them up for compliance; the clerks could not raise a hand against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang compiled every relevant regulation and held the clerks to them so strictly that they could find no leverage against him.

sentences.zh: 以端明殿學士知鄭州，為政有能聲，盜悉竄他境，至夜戶不閉。

translations.literal: As Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance he governed Zheng Prefecture; his administration won a reputation for competence, thieves all fled to other regions, and at night people did not close their doors.
translations.idiomatic: As Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance he governed Zheng Prefecture with such success that thieves fled to neighboring regions and people slept with their doors unlatched at night.

sentences.zh: 嘗有使客亡橐中物，移書詰盜，公亮報：「吾境不藏盜，殆從者之廋耳。

translations.literal: Once an envoy guest lost something from his bag; he sent a letter demanding the thief; Gongliang replied: "Our region does not harbor thieves—likely it is hidden by your attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Once a visiting envoy lost something from his baggage and wrote to demand the thief. Gongliang replied: "My jurisdiction does not harbor thieves—it was likely hidden by one of your attendants."

sentences.zh: 」索之，果然。

translations.literal: They searched for it, and so it was.
translations.idiomatic: A search was made, and so it proved.

sentences.zh: 復入為翰林學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: He returned to court as Hanlin Academician and governed Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Hanlin Academician and Governor of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Supervisor of Remonstrance and Vice Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Supervisor of Remonstrance and Vice Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 加禮部侍郎，除樞密使。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Vice Minister of Rites and appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Rites and appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，拜吏部侍郎、同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiayou he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, Concurrent Grand Counselor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiayou he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, Grand Counselor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 公亮明練文法，更踐久，習知朝廷臺閣典憲，首相韓琦每咨訪焉。

translations.literal: Gongliang was clear and practiced in statutes and regulations; through long service he was thoroughly versed in court and secretariat precedents, and chief minister Han Qi consulted him on each occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang was thoroughly versed in law and precedent; after long service he knew every regulation of court and secretariat, and Chief Minister Han Qi consulted him constantly.

sentences.zh: 仁宗末年，琦請建儲，與公亮等共定大議。

translations.literal: In Renzong's final years Qi requested establishment of an heir, and with Gongliang and others jointly settled the great policy.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's final years Qi proposed establishing an heir, and together with Gongliang and others settled the succession.

sentences.zh: 密州民田產銀，或盜取之，大理當以強。

translations.literal: In Mizhou common people's fields produced silver; some stole it, and the Court of Judicial Review would punish as robbery by force.
translations.idiomatic: In Mizhou some fields yielded silver; when people stole it, the Court of Judicial Review would classify the offense as robbery.

sentences.zh: 公亮曰：「此禁物也，取之雖強，與盜物民家有間矣。

translations.literal: Gongliang said: "This is a prohibited substance; though taking it is by force, it differs from robbing a common household.
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang argued: "Silver is a prohibited substance; though the taking may be forcible, it is not the same as robbing an ordinary household."

sentences.zh: 」固爭之，遂下有司議，比劫禁物法，盜得不死。

translations.literal: He steadfastly contended; the matter was sent down for official deliberation and, by analogy to the law on prohibited goods, the thief was not sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: He argued forcefully until the case was referred for review; by analogy to the law on prohibited goods, the thief escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 初，東州人多用此抵法，自是無死者。

translations.literal: Previously people in the eastern circuits often used this comparison in capital cases; from then on there were no executions.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, eastern circuits had often invoked capital statutes in such cases; after Gongliang's ruling, no one was executed for such offenses.

sentences.zh: 契丹縱人漁界河，又數通鹽舟，吏不敢禁，皆謂與之校，且生事。

translations.literal: The Khitan allowed people to fish in the border river and repeatedly sent salt boats through; officials dared not forbid it, all saying that competing with them would only stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan allowed their people to fish in the border river and repeatedly sent salt boats across it; local officials dared not interfere, saying that pushing back would only provoke trouble.

sentences.zh: 公亮言：「萌芽不禁，後將奈何？

translations.literal: Gongliang said: "If the sprout is not checked, what will be done later?
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang said: "If we fail to check this at the first sign, what will we do when it grows worse?"

sentences.zh: 雄州趙滋勇而有謀，可任也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zi of Xiong Prefecture is brave and resourceful—he can be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zi of Xiong Prefecture is brave and shrewd—he is the man for this.

sentences.zh: 」使諭以指意，邊害訖息。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to convey the intended policy, and border harm ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to convey the court's intent, and the border trouble ended.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，加中書侍郎兼禮部尚書，尋加戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Gongliang was given the additional titles Vice Director of the Secretariat concurrent Minister of Rites, and soon after Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong succeeded, Gongliang was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Rites, and soon after given the additional title of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，遼使至不能見，命公亮宴于館，使者不肯赴，公亮質之曰：「錫宴不赴，是不虔君命也。

translations.literal: When the emperor was ill, Liao envoys arrived and could not have audience; he ordered Gongliang to host a banquet at the guest house; the envoys refused to attend; Gongliang questioned them: "To refuse a bestowed banquet is to be disrespectful of the ruler's command.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Liao envoys arrived but could not have audience; Gongliang was ordered to host them at the guest house. They refused to attend. Gongliang challenged them: "To refuse a banquet granted by the sovereign is to show contempt for his command."

sentences.zh: 人主有疾，而必使親臨，處之安乎？

translations.literal: When the sovereign is ill, yet you insist he must come in person—is that a comfortable way to handle things?
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is ill, yet you insist he must appear in person—is that reasonable?

sentences.zh: 」使者即就席。

translations.literal: The envoys at once took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys immediately took their seats.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，加門下侍郎兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, he was given the additional titles Vice Director of the Chancellery concurrent Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 公亮方厚莊重，沈深周密，平居謹繩墨，蹈規矩；

translations.literal: Gongliang was square, solid, and dignified, deep and thorough in deliberation; in ordinary life he was strict about rule and measure and observed every regulation;
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang was sober, dignified, and deeply deliberative; in ordinary conduct he rigorously observed every rule and regulation;

sentences.zh: 然性吝嗇，殖貨至鉅萬，帝嘗以方張安世。

translations.literal: yet by nature he was stingy and amassed wealth to the amount of tens of thousands; the emperor once compared him to Zhang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was stingy by nature and amassed wealth on a vast scale; the emperor once compared him to Zhang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 初薦王安石，及同輔政，知上方向之，陰為子孫計，凡更張庶事，一切聽順，而外若不與之者。

translations.literal: At first he recommended Wang Anshi; when they served together as counselors he knew the emperor's preference and secretly plotted for his descendants; in every reform and renewal of affairs he acquiesced in all, while outwardly seeming not to go along.
translations.idiomatic: He had early recommended Wang Anshi; once they served together he saw which way the emperor leaned and quietly looked after his family's interests. On every reform he went along entirely, while outwardly seeming to stand apart.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣子孝寬參其謀，至上前略無所異，於是帝益信任安石。

translations.literal: He once sent his son Xiaokuan to join in the planning; before the throne Xiaokuan raised almost no objections—thereupon the emperor trusted Anshi all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent his son Xiaokuan to join Wang's planning sessions; before the throne Xiaokuan raised scarcely any objection, and the emperor's trust in Wang only grew.

sentences.zh: 安石德其助己，故引擢孝寬至樞密以報之。

translations.literal: Anshi was grateful for his help and therefore promoted Xiaokuan to the Bureau of Military Affairs in repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was grateful for this support and in return elevated Xiaokuan to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾嘗從容責公亮不能救正，公亮曰：「上與介甫如一人，此乃天也。

translations.literal: Su Shi once calmly reproached Gongliang for failing to set things right; Gongliang said: "The emperor and Jiefu are like one person—this is Heaven's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi once gently reproached Gongliang for failing to check the reforms. Gongliang replied: "The emperor and Jiefu are as one—this is Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 」世譏其持祿固寵云。

translations.literal: The age mocked him for clinging to salary and securing favor.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mocked him for clinging to office and currying favor.

sentences.zh: 子孝寬，從子孝廣、孝蘊。

translations.literal: His son Xiaokuan; his nephews Xiaoguang and Xiaoyun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiaokuan; his nephews were Xiaoguang and Xiaoyun.

sentences.zh: 子 孝寬

translations.literal: Son: Xiaokuan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xiaokuan

sentences.zh: 孝寬，字令綽，以蔭知桐城縣。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan, styled Lingchuo, by inherited privilege became magistrate of Tongcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan, styled Lingchuo, entered office as magistrate of Tongcheng County through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 選知咸平縣，民詣府訴雨傷麥，府以妄杖之。

translations.literal: Selected and appointed magistrate of Xianping County; the people appealed to the prefecture that rain had damaged the wheat, and the prefect punished them as false accusers.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected and appointed magistrate of Xianping County. When the people appealed to the prefecture that rain had ruined their wheat crop, the prefect had them beaten for making false claims.

sentences.zh: 孝寬躬行田，辨其實，得蠲賦。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan personally walked the fields, verified the truth, and obtained remission of tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan inspected the fields himself, confirmed the damage, and secured a tax remission.

sentences.zh: 除秘閣修撰、提點開封府界鎮縣。

translations.literal: Removed to Compiler at the Palace Archive and Intendant of market towns and counties in the Kaifeng Prefecture jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Compiler at the Palace Archive and Intendant of the market towns and counties within the Kaifeng Prefecture boundary.

sentences.zh: 保甲法行，民相驚言且籍為兵。

translations.literal: When the Baojia system was implemented, the people alarmed one another, saying they would soon be registered as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Baojia system took effect, the people frightened one another with rumors that they would soon be registered for military service.

sentences.zh: 知府韓維上言，乞候農隙行之。

translations.literal: Prefect Han Wei memorialized, requesting that it be carried out during slack agricultural season.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Han Wei memorialized the throne, asking that implementation wait until the farming season had a lull.

sentences.zh: 孝寬牓十七縣，揭賞告捕扇惑者，民兵不敢訴，維之言不得行。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan posted notices in seventeen counties, offering rewards to report and arrest agitators; the militia did not dare appeal, and Wei's words were not put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan posted notices in all seventeen counties offering rewards for reporting and arresting those who stirred up panic. The militia dared not complain, and Wei's proposal went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 入知審官東院、判刑部。

translations.literal: Entered office as Director of the Eastern Court of Judicial Review and concurrent Associate Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He entered central office as Director of the Eastern Court of Judicial Review and Associate Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，遷樞密都承旨，承旨用文臣，自孝寬始。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, he was transferred to Chief Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; civilian officials were used for Chief Director beginning with Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xining he was made Chief Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs—the first time a civilian had held that post, beginning with Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 擢拜樞密直學士、簽書樞密院。

translations.literal: Promoted and appointed Academician in Direct Attendance at the Bureau of Military Affairs and Co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician in Direct Attendance at the Bureau of Military Affairs and Co-signatory of the Bureau.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，除喪，以端明殿學士知河陽，徙鄆。

translations.literal: Mourning his father's death; when the mourning period ended, he was made Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity and prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he entered mourning; after the mourning period he was made Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity and prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鄆有孟子廟，孝寬請於朝，得封鄒國公，配享孔子。

translations.literal: Yan had a temple to Mencius; Xiaokuan petitioned the court and obtained enfeoffment as Duke of Zou, with sacrificial honors accompanying Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Prefecture had a temple to Mencius. Xiaokuan petitioned the court and won for Mencius the title Duke of Zou and a place in sacrificial rites alongside Confucius.

sentences.zh: 連徙鎮，以吏部尚書召，道卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Transferred successively among prefectures; summoned as Minister of Personnel; died en route, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred from one prefecture to another in succession, then summoned back as Minister of Personnel, but died on the road at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 孝廣，字仲錫。

translations.literal: Xiaoguang, styled Zhongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoguang, styled Zhongxi.

sentences.zh: 元豐末，為北外都水丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfeng, he served as Vice Director of the Northern Outer Waterways Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanfeng era he served as Vice Director of the Northern Outer Waterways Office.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，大臣議復河故道，召孝廣問之，言不可，出通判保州。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou, when high ministers debated restoring the river's old course, Xiaoguang was summoned for consultation; he said it could not be done and was sent out as Vice Prefect of Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era, when senior ministers debated restoring the Yellow River to its old channel, Xiaoguang was summoned for his opinion. He argued against the plan and was sent out as Vice Prefect of Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為都水丞。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was again made Director of the Waterways Office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was again appointed Director of the Waterways Office.

sentences.zh: 前此，班行使臣部木筏至者，須校驗無所失亡，乃得送銓，監吏領賕謝，不時遣。

translations.literal: Previously, when envoys on imperial missions arrived escorting raft timber, verification that nothing was lost had to be completed before they could be sent on to the Selection Bureau; supervising clerks accepted bribes in thanks and did not dispatch them promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when envoys on imperial missions arrived with timber rafts in tow, they could not proceed to the Selection Bureau until an inspection confirmed nothing was missing. Supervising clerks took bribes and delayed their departure indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 孝廣治籍疏姓名，謹其去留，一歲中，歸選者百輩。

translations.literal: Xiaoguang organized registers listing names and carefully tracked comings and goings; within one year, a hundred parties returned for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoguang drew up registers with each man's name and strictly tracked arrivals and departures. Within a year, a hundred parties had returned for appointment.

sentences.zh: 除京西轉運判官，入為水部員外郎。

translations.literal: Removed to Fiscal Judge of the Jingxi Circuit; entered office as Vice Director of the Waterways Section, Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Fiscal Judge of the Jingxi Circuit, then entered central office as Vice Director of the Waterways Section in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 河決內黃，詔孝廣行視，遂疏蘇村，鑿鉅野，導河北流，紓澶、滑、深、瀛之害。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst at Neihuang; an edict ordered Xiaoguang to inspect on site; he then dredged Sucun, cut Juanye, and channeled the river's northern flow, easing the damage at Chan, Hua, Shen, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke through at Neihuang, an edict ordered Xiaoguang to inspect the breach. He dredged Sucun, cut through Juanye, and redirected the northern stream, relieving the flooding at Chan, Hua, Shen, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 遷都水使者。

translations.literal: Promoted to Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 洛水頻歲湓湧，浸齧北岸，孝廣按河堤，得廢澾口遺跡，曰：「此昔人所以殺水勢也。

translations.literal: The Luo River had swollen and surged year after year, eroding the north bank; Xiaoguang inspected the river dikes and found traces of an abandoned outlet, saying: "This is how men of old reduced the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: The Luo River had swollen year after year, gnawing at the north bank. Xiaoguang inspected the dikes, found the remains of an abandoned sluice, and said, "This is how our predecessors tamed the flood.

sentences.zh: 」即日浚決之，累石為防，自是無水患。

translations.literal: " That same day he dredged and opened it, piled stones for a barrier, and from then on there were no floods.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he dredged the outlet open, piled stones into a barrier, and from then on the river gave no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 出提點永興路刑獄，陝西、京西轉運副使，還為左司郎中，擢戶部侍郎，進尚書。

translations.literal: Sent out as Judicial Intendant of Yongxing Circuit; made Vice Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi and Jingxi circuits; returned as Director of the Left Section; promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and then Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Judicial Intendant of Yongxing Circuit, then Vice Transport Commissioner for Shaanxi and Jingxi. Recalled to the capital, he rose from Director of the Left Section to Vice Minister of Revenue and then Minister.

sentences.zh: 坐錢帛不給費，罷為天章閣待制、知杭州。

translations.literal: Found guilty because funds and cloth were not disbursed; dismissed to Academician without specific assignment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished because funds and cloth had not been disbursed on schedule, demoted to Academician without assignment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, and sent out as prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以前聘契丹失奉使體，奪職。

translations.literal: Also stripped of rank for having failed to observe proper embassy deportment on a mission to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He was also stripped of rank for impropriety on an earlier mission to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 尋復之，移知潭州，加顯謨閣直學士、知鄆州。

translations.literal: Soon restored; transferred to prefect of Tanzhou; given the additional title Academician in Direct Attendance at the Hall of Manifest Worthies and prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his rank was restored. He was transferred to Tanzhou, then given the title Academician in Direct Attendance at the Hall of Manifest Worthies and made prefect of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝廣與胡安國、鄒浩善，皆大觀中忤時相，御史論之，復奪職知饒州。

translations.literal: Xiaoguang was on good terms with Hu Anguo and Zou Hao; all three offended the chief minister during the Daguan era; censors impeached them and he was again stripped of rank and made prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoguang was close to Hu Anguo and Zou Hao. All three had crossed the chief minister during the Daguan era. When censors impeached them, Xiaoguang was again demoted and sent out as prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，徙廣州，歷成德軍、太原府，得故職以卒，年六十，贈正議大夫。

translations.literal: After a year, transferred to Guangzhou; served at Chengde Army and Taiyuan Prefecture; recovered his former rank and died, aged sixty; posthumously awarded Grand Master of Rectifying Governance.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Guangzhou, then served at Chengde Army and Taiyuan Prefecture. He recovered his former rank before he died at sixty and was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Rectifying Governance.

sentences.zh: 孝廣涖官以嚴稱，獲盜，輒碎其手焉。

translations.literal: Xiaoguang was known for severity in office; when thieves were caught, he would smash their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoguang was famed for harsh rule. When thieves were caught, he had their hands broken.

sentences.zh: 孝蘊，字處善。

translations.literal: Xiaoyun, styled Chushan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyun, styled Chushan.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，管幹發運司糶糴事，建言揚之瓜洲，潤之京口，常之奔牛，易堰為閘，以便漕運、商賈。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng, he managed grain sale and purchase affairs of the Transport Office; he proposed that at Guazhou in Yangzhou, Jingkou in Run, and Benniu in Chang, weirs be replaced with locks to facilitate grain transport and merchants.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era he oversaw grain sale and purchase for the Transport Office. He proposed replacing weirs with locks at Guazhou in Yang Prefecture, Jingkou in Run Prefecture, and Benniu in Chang Prefecture to ease grain transport and trade.

sentences.zh: 既成，公私便之。

translations.literal: Once completed, both government and private interests benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Once the work was finished, officials and merchants alike found it a great convenience.

sentences.zh: 提舉兩浙常平，改轉運判官，知臨江軍，召為左司員外郎，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: Intendant of the Zhejiang East and West Ever-Normal Granaries; changed to Fiscal Judge; prefect of Linjiang Army; summoned as Vice Director of the Left Section; promoted to Attendant at the Office for Recording the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Intendant of the Two-Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries, then as Fiscal Judge and prefect of Linjiang Army. Recalled to court, he became Vice Director of the Left Section and then Attendant at the Office for Recording the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 時京邑有盜，徽宗怒，期三日不獲，坐尹罪。

translations.literal: At the time there were robbers in the capital; Emperor Huizong was angry and set a three-day deadline for capture—failure would hold the metropolitan prefect accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers were active in the capital, and Emperor Huizong was furious. He gave the metropolitan prefect three days to catch them—or face punishment himself.

sentences.zh: 孝蘊奏：「求盜急則遁益遠，小緩當自出。

translations.literal: Xiaoyun memorialized: "If the search for robbers is too urgent they flee still farther; if slightly relaxed they will emerge on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyun memorialized: "Press the hunt too hard and the robbers flee farther away; ease off a little and they will show themselves.

sentences.zh: 」從其言，得盜。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his advice and the robbers were caught.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took his advice, and the robbers were caught.

sentences.zh: 崇寧建殿中省，擢為監。

translations.literal: When the Directorate Within the Hall was established in Chongning, he was promoted to its Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate Within the Hall was created in the Chongning era, he was made its Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 居數月，言者論其與張商英善，以集賢殿修撰出知襄州，徙江浙荊淮發運。

translations.literal: After several months, critics argued his friendship with Zhang Shangying; he was sent out as Compiler at the Hall for Gathering Worthies and prefect of Xiangzhou, then transferred to Jiang-Zhe-Huai transport.
translations.idiomatic: Within months, critics charged that he was close to Zhang Shangying. He was sent out as Compiler at the Hall for Gathering Worthies and prefect of Xiangzhou, then transferred to the Jiang-Zhe-Huai Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 泗州議開直河，以避漲溢沙石之害，孝蘊以淮、汴不相接，不可成。

translations.literal: Sizhou debated opening a straight channel to avoid damage from floods, sand, and stone; Xiaoyun argued that the Huai and Bian rivers did not connect and the project could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At Sizhou officials proposed cutting a straight channel to escape flood damage from sand and gravel. Xiaoyun argued that the Huai and Bian did not join and the work could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 既而工役大集，竟成之，策勳第賞，辭不受。

translations.literal: Before long labor was massed and it was completed; ranked for merit and reward; he declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Before long laborers were massed and the channel was finished. He was ranked for merit and offered reward, but declined.

sentences.zh: 未幾，河果塞，召為戶部侍郎，帝嘗問右曹儲物幾何，疾作不能對。

translations.literal: Before long the river indeed silted up; summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue; the emperor once asked how much was stored in the right office; illness struck and he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the river did silt shut, just as he had warned. Recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue, he was once asked how much the right office held in store—but illness seized him and he could not reply.

sentences.zh: 徙工部，以顯謨閣待制知杭州。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Works; made Academician without specific assignment at the Hall of Manifest Worthies and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Works, then made Academician without assignment at the Hall of Manifest Worthies and sent out as prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後坐累，連削黜，至貶安遠軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Afterwards punished in succession, demoted repeatedly, finally exiled as Vice Military Commissioner of Anyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was punished again and again, stripped of rank step by step, until he was exiled as Vice Military Commissioner of Anyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，始復天章閣待制、知歙州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe, restored at last to Academician without assignment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and prefect of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuanhe he was at last restored to Academician without assignment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and made prefect of She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 方臘起青溪，孝蘊約敕郡內，無得奔擾，分兵守厄塞，有避賊來歸者，獲罪，使出境，人稍恃以安。

translations.literal: When Fang La rose at Qingxi, Xiaoyun ordered the prefecture not to scatter in panic, posted troops at strategic passes, and punished those who fled the bandits and then returned—so the people grew somewhat secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La rebelled at Qingxi, Xiaoyun ordered the prefecture to hold steady and not flee in panic. He posted troops at the passes and punished anyone who had run from the rebels and then tried to return, and the people gradually felt safer.

sentences.zh: 會移青州，既行而歙陷，道改杭州，時賊已破杭，孝蘊單車至城下。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to Qingzhou, he had already set out when She fell; en route his assignment was changed to Hangzhou, and by then the rebels had already taken the city; Xiaoyun came alone to the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qingzhou and had already departed when She Prefecture fell. En route his orders were changed to Hangzhou—but the rebels had already seized the city. Xiaoyun rode alone to the gate.

sentences.zh: 城既克復，軍士多殺人，孝蘊下令，脅從者得自首，無輒殺，皆束手不敢驁。

translations.literal: After the city was recovered, soldiers killed many people; Xiaoyun issued an order that those who had been coerced could surrender themselves, and that no one was to be killed arbitrarily; all restrained themselves and did not riot.
translations.idiomatic: After the city was retaken, the troops killed many people. Xiaoyun ordered that those who had been forced to follow the rebels could turn themselves in, and that no one was to be killed without cause. The soldiers held back and dared not run wild.

sentences.zh: 論功，進顯謨閣直學士，又加龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: For merit, promoted to Academician in Direct Attendance at the Hall of Manifest Worthies, then also given the title Academician at the Hall of Imperial Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Academician in Direct Attendance at the Hall of Manifest Worthies, then also made Academician at the Hall of Imperial Dragon.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈通議大夫。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-five; posthumously awarded Grand Master of Discussion and Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Discussion and Governance.

sentences.zh: 陳升之

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengzhi

sentences.zh: 陳升之，字暘叔，建州建陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi, styled Yangshu, was a man of Jianyang in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengzhi, styled Yangshu, was a native of Jianyang in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，歷知封州、漢陽軍，入為監察御史、右司諫，改起居舍人、知諫院。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served successively as prefect of Feng Prefecture and Hanyang Military Prefecture; entered office as Investigating Censor and Remonstrator of the Right Bureau; changed to Attendant at the Office for Recording the Emperor's Actions and Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as prefect of Feng Prefecture and Hanyang Military Prefecture in turn. He entered court as Investigating Censor and Remonstrator of the Right Bureau, then became Attendant at the Office for Recording the Emperor's Actions and Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時俗好藏去交親尺牘，有訟，則轉相告言，有司據以推詰。

translations.literal: The custom of the time favored hiding away letters from friends and relatives; when lawsuits arose, people informed on one another, and officials interrogated on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: It was then the fashion to hoard letters from friends and kin. When disputes arose, people denounced one another, and officials built their cases on such testimony.

sentences.zh: 升之謂：「此告訐之習也，請禁止之。

translations.literal: Shengzhi said: "This is the habit of informing and denouncing; I request that it be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi said, "This is the habit of tale-bearing and denunciation. I ask that it be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「三館為搢紳華途，近者用人益輕，遂為貴遊進取之階，請嚴其選。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The Three Academies are the splendid path of the gentry; lately appointments have grown ever lighter, until the posts became a ladder for the privileged to advance; I request that selection be tightened.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The Three Academies are the crown of a gentleman's career, yet lately appointments have grown ever more casual until the posts became a ladder for well-connected climbers. Selection should be made strict.

sentences.zh: 」詔自今臣僚乞子孫恩者，毋得除館閣。

translations.literal: " An edict followed: from now on, when officials petitioned favor for their descendants, they were not to be appointed to the Academies and Archives.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict followed: from then on, when officials sought appointments for their sons and grandsons, those posts could not be in the Academies and Archives.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎王瓘遇殿帥郭承祐於道，訶怒不下馬，執送府。

translations.literal: Associate Compiler Wang Guan encountered Palace Guard Commander Guo Chengyou on the road, angrily berated him for not dismounting, and had him escorted to the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Compiler Wang Guan met Palace Guard Commander Guo Chengyou on the road, berated him for failing to dismount, and had him taken to the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 升之言京官不宜為節度使下馬，因劾承祐驕恣，解其任。

translations.literal: Shengzhi said that capital officials ought not to dismount for a military commissioner; he therefore impeached Chengyou for arrogance and removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi argued that capital officials should not dismount for a military commissioner. He impeached Chengyou for insolence and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 張堯佐緣後宮親，為三司使，尋為宣徽使；

translations.literal: Zhang Yaozuo, by connection with the inner palace, became Commissioner of the Three Departments, and soon Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yaozuo, through ties to the inner palace, became Commissioner of the Three Departments and soon Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service;

sentences.zh: 內侍王守忠領兩鎮留後，求升正班；

translations.literal: the inner attendant Wang Shouzhong held regency over two circuits and sought promotion to the regular official roster;
translations.idiomatic: the inner attendant Wang Shouzhong held regency over two circuits and sought promotion to the regular official roster;

sentences.zh: 御史張昪補郡，久不召；

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Bian was assigned to a prefecture and long went without recall;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Bian was sent to a prefecture and long went without recall;

sentences.zh: 彭思永論事，令窮問所從來；

translations.literal: Peng Siyong remonstrated on policy and was ordered to be exhaustively questioned as to his sources;
translations.idiomatic: Peng Siyong remonstrated on policy and was ordered interrogated as to where his information came from;

sentences.zh: 唐介擊宰相，斥嶺南：升之皆極諫。

translations.literal: Tang Jie attacked the chief minister and was banished to the far south: Shengzhi remonstrated to the utmost on all these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jie assailed the chief minister and was exiled to the far south—on all these matters Shengzhi remonstrated to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Promoted to Associate Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Associate Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 凡任言責五年，所上數十百事，然持論不堅，以故不盡施用。

translations.literal: In all, he held remonstrance responsibility for five years and submitted several dozen or a hundred items, yet because his arguments were not firm, they were not fully put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: For five years he bore remonstrance responsibility and submitted scores of memorials, yet his arguments lacked force and many were never fully adopted.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、河北都轉運使，知瀛州、真定府，加龍圖閣直學士，復知諫院。

translations.literal: Promoted to Academician without assignment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and Hebei Transport Commissioner; prefect of Ying Prefecture and Zhending Prefecture; given the additional title Academician in Direct Attendance at the Hall of Imperial Dragon; again Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician without assignment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and made Hebei Transport Commissioner, then prefect of Ying and Zhending. Given the title Academician in Direct Attendance at the Hall of Imperial Dragon, he again headed the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上言：「天下州縣治否，朝廷不能周知，悉付之轉運使。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Whether prefectures and counties throughout the realm are well governed, the court cannot know in full detail, and entrusts all to transport commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The court cannot keep watch over every prefecture and county in the realm and has entrusted that judgment entirely to transport commissioners.

sentences.zh: 今選用不精，又無考課，非闇滯罷懦，則淩肆刻薄，所以疾苦愁歎，雍圩上聞。

translations.literal: Now selection is not careful, and there is no performance review; if they are not dim, stagnant, dismissed, or timid, then they are overbearing and harsh—therefore suffering, distress, and sighs are blocked from reaching the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments are careless and there is no review. The incompetent and timid alternate with the arrogant and cruel—and the people's grief never reaches the throne.

sentences.zh: 必欲垂意元元，宜從此始。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to care for the common people, you should begin here.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to care for the common people, this is where to begin.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔翰林學士承旨孫抃、權御史中丞張昪，與升之同領磨勘轉運使及提點刑獄功務。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict ordered Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Sun Bian and Acting Censor-in-Chief Zhang Bian, together with Shengzhi, jointly to conduct merit review of transport commissioners and judicial intendants.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then ordered Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Sun Bian and Acting Censor-in-Chief Zhang Bian, together with Shengzhi, to conduct a joint merit review of transport commissioners and judicial intendants.

sentences.zh: 升之初為諫官時，嘗請抑絕內降，詔許有司執奏勿下。

translations.literal: When Shengzhi first served as remonstrator, he had once requested strict curbing of inner edicts; an edict had permitted responsible offices to memorialize in opposition and not implement them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzhi first served as remonstrator, he had asked that inner edicts be strictly curbed; the throne had then permitted responsible offices to resist them by memorial.

sentences.zh: 至是，申言之。

translations.literal: At this time he raised the matter again.
translations.idiomatic: Now he raised the issue again.

sentences.zh: 詔委三省劾正其罪，仍揭於朝堂。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Departments to investigate and correct the offense, and the matter was posted in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Three Departments to investigate and punish the offense, and the decree was posted in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 文彥博乞罷相，升之慮樞密使賈昌朝復用，疏論其邪，昌朝卒罷去。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo asked to resign as chief minister; Shengzhi feared that Military Affairs Commissioner Jia Changchao would be reappointed; he submitted a memorial on Changchao's wickedness, and Changchao was ultimately dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yanbo asked to resign as chief minister, Shengzhi feared Jia Changchao would be restored to the Bureau of Military Affairs. He memorialized against Changchao's corruption, and Changchao was finally removed.

sentences.zh: 遷樞密直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: Promoted to Academician in Direct Attendance at the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician in Direct Attendance at the Bureau of Military Affairs and made prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year, appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是諫官御史唐介、范師道、呂誨、趙抃、王陶交章論升之陰結宦者，故得大用。

translations.literal: Thereupon remonstrators and censors Tang Jie, Fan Shidao, Lü Hui, Zhao Bian, and Wang Tao submitted successive memorials arguing that Shengzhi had secretly allied with eunuchs and therefore obtained great appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators and censors Tang Jie, Fan Shidao, Lü Hui, Zhao Bian, and Wang Tao then submitted memorial after memorial charging that Shengzhi had secretly colluded with eunuchs to win high office.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以示升之，升之丐去。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong showed the memorials to Shengzhi; Shengzhi begged to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong showed the memorials to Shengzhi, who asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝謂輔臣曰：「朕選用執政，豈容內臣預議邪。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his counselors: "When I choose and appoint the chief administration, how can inner attendants be allowed to take part in deliberation?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his counselors, "When I choose men for the chief administration, how can palace eunuchs be allowed a voice in it?

sentences.zh: 」乃兩罷之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon both sides were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " Both Shengzhi and the remonstrators were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以升之為資政殿學士、知定州，徙太原府。

translations.literal: Shengzhi was made Academician at the Hall of Literary Glory and prefect of Dingzhou, then transferred to Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi was made Academician at the Hall of Literary Glory and prefect of Dingzhou, then transferred to Taiyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，復拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, again appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiping he was again made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，以母老請郡，為觀文殿學士、知越州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, he requested a prefectural post because his mother was old; he was made Academician at the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, he asked for a provincial post to care for his aged mother and was made Academician at the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 熙甯元年，徙許，中道改大名府，過闕，留知樞密院。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, transferred to Xu Prefecture; en route changed to Daming Prefecture; passing the capital, he was retained to direct the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining he was transferred to Xu Prefecture, then reassigned en route to Daming. Passing the capital, he was kept on to direct the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 故事，樞密使與知院事不並置。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Military Affairs Commissioner and the Director of the Bureau were not appointed concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Military Affairs Commissioner and the Director of the Bureau were not appointed at the same time.

sentences.zh: 時文彥博、呂公著既為使，帝以升之三輔政，欲稍異其禮，故特命之。

translations.literal: At the time Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongzhu were already commissioners; the emperor, because Shengzhi was one of the three chief administrators, wished to distinguish his rites slightly, and therefore specially appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongzhu were already commissioners. Because Shengzhi was one of the three chief administrators, the emperor wished to mark his status slightly apart and made a special appointment.

sentences.zh: 明年，同制置三司條例司，與王安石共事。

translations.literal: The next year, jointly directed the Three Departments Regulations Office and worked with Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he jointly directed the Three Departments Regulations Office and worked alongside Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 數月，拜中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: Within several months, appointed Grand Counselor, Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Grand Academician at the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was made Grand Counselor, Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Grand Academician at the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

sentences.zh: 升之既相，遂請免條例司，其說以為宰相無所不統，所領職事，豈可稱司。

translations.literal: Once Shengzhi became chief minister, he requested abolition of the Regulations Office; his reasoning was that the chief minister oversees all and the duties he heads ought not be called an office.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shengzhi became chief minister, he asked to abolish the Regulations Office. A prime minister, he argued, oversaw everything; the duties he headed should not be styled an "office."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「古之六卿，即今之執政，有司馬、司徒、司空，各名一職，何害於理？

translations.literal: Anshi said: "The six ministers of antiquity are today's chief administrators—there were Minister of War, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works, each naming one duty; what harm is there to principle?
translations.idiomatic: Wang said, "The six ministers of antiquity are today's chief administrators. There were the Minister of War, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works—each with a distinct charge. Where is the harm in that?

sentences.zh: 」升之曰：「若制置百司條例則可，但今制置三司一官，則不可。

translations.literal: " Shengzhi said: "If it were to regulate the statutes of the hundred offices, that would be acceptable; but to regulate only the Three Departments as one office—that cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi replied, "Regulating the statutes of every office would be one thing. To set up an office for the Three Departments alone—that will not do.

sentences.zh: 」由是忤安石，稱疾歸臥逾十旬，帝數敦諭，乃出。

translations.literal: " Thereby he offended Anshi; he pleaded illness and retired to bed for more than a hundred days; the emperor repeatedly urged him, and only then did he emerge.
translations.idiomatic: This put him at odds with Wang. He pleaded illness and kept to his bed for more than three months. Only after repeated imperial urging did he return to court.

sentences.zh: 會母喪，去位；

translations.literal: When his mother died, he left office;
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he left office;

sentences.zh: 終制，召為樞密使。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was summoned as Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned back as Military Affairs Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 足疾不能立朝，七年，冬祀，又不能相禮。

translations.literal: A foot ailment kept him from standing at court; in the seventh year, at the winter sacrifice, he could not again preside over the rites.
translations.idiomatic: A foot ailment kept him from standing at court. In the seventh year, at the winter sacrifice, he could no longer preside over the rites.

sentences.zh: 拜鎮江軍節度使、同平章事、判揚州，封秀國公。

translations.literal: Appointed Military Commissioner of Zhenjiang Army, concurrent Grand Counselor, overseer of Yangzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Xiuguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Commissioner of Zhenjiang Army, concurrent Grand Counselor, overseer of Yangzhou, and enfeoffed Duke of Xiuguo.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太保、中書令，諡曰成肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor and Grand Master of the Palace, with posthumous title Cheng Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor and Grand Master of the Palace, with the posthumous title Cheng Su.

sentences.zh: 升之深狡多數，善傅會以取富貴。

translations.literal: Shengzhi was deeply cunning and scheming, adept at twisting circumstances to win wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi was deeply cunning, skilled at twisting facts to suit the moment and win wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 王安石用事，患正論盈庭，引升之自助。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held power, troubled that upright discourse filled the court, he brought in Shengzhi to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi held power, troubled by the upright discourse that filled the court, he brought in Shengzhi to bolster his position.

sentences.zh: 升之心知其不可，而竭力為之用，安石德之，故使先己為相。

translations.literal: Shengzhi knew in his heart it could not succeed, yet exerted himself to serve Wang's aims; Wang was grateful and therefore had him made chief minister before himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi knew in his heart the reforms could not succeed, yet he worked tirelessly for Wang—and Wang, grateful, had him made chief minister before taking the post himself.

sentences.zh: 甫得志，即求解條例司，又時為小異，陽若不與之同者。

translations.literal: As soon as he had gotten his wish, he at once requested abolition of the Regulations Office, and from time to time offered minor dissent, openly pretending not to agree with Wang.
translations.idiomatic: The moment he had what he wanted, he asked to abolish the Regulations Office and from time to time offered minor objections, openly pretending not to agree with Wang.

sentences.zh: 世以是譏之，謂之「筌相」。

translations.literal: The world mocked him for this, calling him the "Basket Prime Minister."
translations.idiomatic: The world mocked him for this and called him the "Fish-Trap Prime Minister."

sentences.zh: 升之初名旭，避神宗嫌名，改焉。

translations.literal: Shengzhi's original name was Xu; to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Shenzong, he changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi's original name was Xu; to avoid the taboo of Emperor Shenzong's name, he changed it.

sentences.zh: 吳充，字沖卿，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Wu Chong, styled Chongqing, was a man of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong, styled Chongqing, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未冠舉進士，與兄育、京、方皆高第。

translations.literal: Before coming of age he passed the jinshi examination; he and his elder brothers Yu, Jing, and Fang all placed at the top of their cohorts.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he passed the jinshi examination; he and his elder brothers Yu, Jing, and Fang all graduated at the top of their cohorts.

sentences.zh: 調穀熟主簿，入為國子監直講、吳王宮教授。

translations.literal: Assigned as registrar of Gushu County; entered office as Direct Lecturer at the Directorate of Education and Instructor at the Prince of Wu's palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as registrar of Gushu County, then entered office as Direct Lecturer at the Directorate of Education and Instructor at the Prince of Wu's palace.

sentences.zh: 等輩多與宗室狎，充齒最少，獨以嚴見憚，相率設席受經。

translations.literal: His peers for the most part were familiar with the imperial clansmen; Chong was the youngest, yet alone was regarded with awe for his severity—they all lined up to set out mats and receive his instruction.
translations.idiomatic: His peers were mostly on familiar terms with the imperial clansmen. Chong was the youngest, yet alone was feared for his severity—they all lined up to set out mats and receive his instruction.

sentences.zh: 充作《六箴》以獻，曰視，曰聽，曰好，曰學，曰進德，曰崇儉。

translations.literal: Chong composed the "Six Admonitions" and presented them, on vision, hearing, preferences, learning, advancing in virtue, and cherishing frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Chong composed the "Six Admonitions" and presented them, on vision, hearing, preferences, learning, advancing in virtue, and cherishing frugality.

sentences.zh: 仁宗命繕寫賜皇族，英宗在藩邸，書之坐右。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong ordered them copied and bestowed upon the imperial clan; when Emperor Yingzong was still in his princely residence, he placed the text at his right hand.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong ordered them copied and bestowed upon the imperial clan. When Emperor Yingzong was still in his princely residence, he kept the text at his right hand.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，數問充所在，會入覲，語其為吳王宮教授時事，嘉勞之。

translations.literal: When Yingzong succeeded, he repeatedly asked where Chong was; when Chong came to court, the emperor spoke of his time as instructor at the Prince of Wu's palace and praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong succeeded, he repeatedly asked where Chong was. When Chong came to court, the emperor spoke of his time as instructor at the Prince of Wu's palace and praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 尋權鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Acting Vice Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Acting Vice Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.

sentences.zh: 熙甯元年，知制誥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, made Drafting Officer for Proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining he was made Drafting Officer for Proclamations.

sentences.zh: 神宗諭以任用意，曰：「先帝知卿久矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong instructed him to use his own judgment, saying: "The previous emperor knew you long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong told him to use his own judgment, saying, "The previous emperor knew you well for a long time.

sentences.zh: 」遂同知諫院。

translations.literal: " He was then made Associate Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then made Associate Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 言：「士大夫親沒，或藁殯數十年，傷敗風化，宜限期使葬。

translations.literal: He said: "When a scholar-official's parent dies, some leave the body in a rough coffin for decades—this harms and corrupts custom; a deadline should be set requiring burial.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "When a scholar-official's parent dies, some leave the body in a rough coffin for decades. This corrupts public morals, and a deadline should be set requiring burial.

sentences.zh: 」詔著為令。

translations.literal: " An edict codified this as law.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict codified this as law.

sentences.zh: 河北水災、地震，為安撫使。

translations.literal: When Hebei suffered floods and earthquakes, he served as Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei suffered floods and earthquakes, he served as Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 使還，王安石參知政事，充子安持，其婿也，引嫌解諫職，知審刑院，權三司使，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: On returning from his mission, Wang Anshi was Vice Grand Counselor; Chong's son Anch was Wang's son-in-law, so citing conflict of interest he resigned his remonstrance post, became Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Acting Commissioner of the Three Departments, and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission, Wang Anshi was Vice Grand Counselor. Chong's son Anch was Wang's son-in-law, so citing conflict of interest he resigned his remonstrance post and became Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Acting Commissioner of the Three Departments, and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the third year, appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 王韶取洮州，蕃酋木征遁去，充請招還故地，縻以爵秩，使自領所部，永為外臣，無庸列置郡縣，殫財屈力。

translations.literal: When Wang Shao took Taozhou and the tribal chieftain Muzheng fled, Chong requested that he be enticed back to his former lands, bound with titles and ranks, and allowed to rule his own people as a permanent outer vassal—there would be no need to establish prefectures and counties, exhausting finances and straining resources.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shao took Taozhou and the tribal chieftain Muzheng fled, Chong asked that he be enticed back to his former lands, bound with titles and ranks, and allowed to rule his own people as a permanent outer vassal—without establishing prefectures and counties that would exhaust finances and strain the state.

sentences.zh: 時方以開拓付韶，充言不用。

translations.literal: At the time expansion was entrusted to Shao; Chong's proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Expansion had just been entrusted to Shao, and Chong's proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 八年，進檢校太傅、樞密使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor and Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor and Military Affairs Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 充雖與安石連姻，而心不善其所為，數為帝言政事不便。

translations.literal: Although Chong was connected to Anshi by marriage, in his heart he disapproved of what Wang did and repeatedly told the emperor that the administration's policies were harmful.
translations.idiomatic: Although Chong was connected to Wang by marriage, in his heart he disapproved of Wang's policies and repeatedly told the emperor that the administration was doing harm.

sentences.zh: 帝察其中立無與，欲相之，安石去，遂代為同中書門下平章事、監修國史。

translations.literal: The emperor saw that he stood apart without partisan alliance and wished to make him chief minister; when Anshi departed, Chong succeeded him as Grand Counselor, Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Supervisor of State History.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw that he stood apart without partisan ties and wished to make him chief minister. When Wang departed, Chong succeeded him as Grand Counselor, Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Supervisor of State History.

sentences.zh: 充欲有所變革，乞召還司馬光、呂公著、韓維、蘇頌，乃薦孫覺、李常、程顥等數十人。

translations.literal: Chong wished to institute reforms and requested recall of Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, Han Wei, and Su Song; he also recommended several dozen men including Sun Jue, Li Chang, and Cheng Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Chong wished to institute reforms and asked that Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, Han Wei, and Su Song be recalled. He also recommended several dozen men including Sun Jue, Li Chang, and Cheng Hao.

sentences.zh: 光亦以充可告語，與之書曰：「自新法之行，中外洶洶。

translations.literal: Guang also believed Chong could be spoken to frankly and wrote him: "Since the new laws took effect, within and without the court there has been uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also believed Chong could be spoken to frankly and wrote him: "Since the new laws took effect, the court and the country alike have been in uproar.

sentences.zh: 民困於煩苛，迫於誅斂，愁怨流離，轉死溝壑。

translations.literal: The people are worn down by petty severity, pressed by harsh levies, filled with grief and resentment, driven into exile, dying by the roadside in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: The people are worn down by petty severity and harsh levies, filled with grief and resentment, driven into exile, dying in ditches by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 日夜引領，冀朝廷覺悟，一變敝法，幾年於茲矣。

translations.literal: Day and night one stretches one's neck, hoping the court will awaken and transform these bad laws at a stroke—and years have passed thus.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night one stretches one's neck, hoping the court will awaken and transform these bad laws at a stroke—and years have passed in vain.

sentences.zh: 今日救天下之急，苟不罷青苗、免役、保甲、市易，息征伐之謀，而欲求成效，猶惡湯之沸，而益薪鼓橐也。

translations.literal: To save the realm today from urgent peril, if you do not abolish Green Sprouts, exemption-from-corvée, Baojia, and Market Exchange, and abandon plans for military campaigns, yet seek results—it is like detesting boiling soup while adding fuel and fanning the bellows.
translations.idiomatic: To save the realm from its urgent peril today, if you do not abolish Green Sprouts, exemption-from-corvée, Baojia, and Market Exchange, and abandon plans for military campaigns, yet seek results—it is like detesting boiling soup while adding fuel and fanning the bellows.

sentences.zh: 欲去此五者，必先別利害，以悟人主之心。

translations.literal: To abolish these five things, one must first sort out harm and benefit so as to awaken the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: To abolish these five policies, one must first sort out harm and benefit so as to awaken the ruler's heart.

sentences.zh: 欲悟人主之心，必先開言路。

translations.literal: To awaken the ruler's heart, one must first open the channels of discourse.
translations.idiomatic: To awaken the ruler's heart, one must first open the channels of discourse.

sentences.zh: 今病雖已深，猶未至膏肓，失今不治，遂為痼疾矣。

translations.literal: Though the illness is already deep, it has not yet reached the vital core; if it is not treated now, it will become an incurable malady.
translations.idiomatic: Though the illness is already deep, it has not yet reached the vital core. If it is not treated now, it will become incurable.

sentences.zh: 」充不能用。

translations.literal: " Chong could not act on this.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong could not act on this.

sentences.zh: 王珪與充並相，忌充，陰掣其肘。

translations.literal: Wang Gui was chief minister alongside Chong and envied him, secretly restraining him at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui served as chief minister alongside Chong, envied him, and secretly held him back at every turn.

sentences.zh: 而充素惡蔡確，確治相州獄，捕安持及親戚、官屬考治，欲鉤致充語，帝獨明其亡他。

translations.literal: Chong had long disliked Cai Que; Que was investigating a case in Xiang Prefecture, arrested Anch and relatives and subordinates for interrogation, seeking to hook out incriminating words from Chong—but the emperor alone saw that Chong had no other involvement.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had long disliked Cai Que. Que was investigating a case in Xiang Prefecture, arrested Anch and relatives and subordinates for interrogation, and sought to implicate Chong—but the emperor alone saw that Chong had no other involvement.

sentences.zh: 及確預政，充與議變法於前，數為所詘。

translations.literal: When Que entered the chief administration, Chong debated policy reforms with him at court and was repeatedly refuted.
translations.idiomatic: When Que entered the chief administration, Chong debated policy reforms with him at court and was repeatedly refuted.

sentences.zh: 安南師出無功，知諫院張璪又謂充與郭逵書，止其進兵，復置獄。

translations.literal: The Annam campaign had failed without result; Zhang Can, Director of the Remonstrance Bureau, also claimed Chong had written to Guo Kui ordering him to halt his advance, and the case was reopened.
translations.idiomatic: The Annam campaign had failed without result. Zhang Can, Director of the Remonstrance Bureau, also claimed Chong had written to Guo Kui ordering him to halt his advance, and the case was reopened.

sentences.zh: 充既數遭同列困毀，素病瘤，積憂畏，疾益侵。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly suffered obstruction and slander from colleagues, and chronically ill with a tumor, he accumulated worry and fear, and his illness grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Having repeatedly suffered obstruction and slander from colleagues, and chronically ill with a tumor, he accumulated worry and fear until his illness grew worse.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年三月，輿歸第，罷為觀文殿大學士、西太一宮使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Yuanfeng, he was carried home; dismissed to Grand Academician at the Hall for Viewing Literature and Director of the Western Supreme Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Yuanfeng he was carried home, dismissed to Grand Academician at the Hall for Viewing Literature and Director of the Western Supreme Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 逾月，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: After more than a month he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈司空兼侍中，諡曰正憲。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Minister of Works concurrent with Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Zheng Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Works concurrent with Palace Attendant, with the posthumous title Zheng Xian.

sentences.zh: 充內行修飭，事兄甚謹。

translations.literal: In private conduct Chong was disciplined and careful, serving his elder brothers with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: In private life Chong was disciplined and careful, serving his elder brothers with great respect.

sentences.zh: 為相務安靜。

translations.literal: As chief minister he strove above all for quiet stability.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he strove above all for quiet stability.

sentences.zh: 性沉密，對家人語，未嘗及國家事，所言於上，人莫知者。
