translations.literal: His nature was deep and secretive; speaking to his family, he never touched on state affairs, and what he said to the emperor no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was deep and secretive. Speaking to his family, he never touched on state affairs, and what he said to the emperor no one else knew.

sentences.zh: 將終，戒妻子勿以私事干朝廷，帝益悲之。

translations.literal: Near death he admonished wife and children not to import private business into the court, and the emperor was all the more grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he admonished wife and children not to import private business into the court, and the emperor was all the more grieved.

sentences.zh: 世謂充心正而力不足，譏其知不可而弗能勇退也。

translations.literal: The world said Chong's heart was upright but his strength insufficient, mocking him for knowing what was wrong yet being unable to withdraw boldly.
translations.idiomatic: The world said Chong's heart was upright but his strength insufficient, mocking him for knowing what was wrong yet lacking the courage to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 子安詩、安持。

translations.literal: His sons were Anshi and Anch.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Anshi and Anch.

sentences.zh: 安詩在元祐時為諫官、起居郎。

translations.literal: Anshi served in the Yuanyou era as remonstrator and Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi served in the Yuanyou era as remonstrator and Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 安持為都水使者，遷工部侍郎，終天章閣待制。

translations.literal: Anch was Commissioner of Waterways, promoted to Vice Minister of Works, and ended as Academician without assignment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: Anch was Commissioner of Waterways, promoted to Vice Minister of Works, and ended his career as Academician without assignment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations.

sentences.zh: 安詩子儲、安持子侔，官皆員外郎，坐與妖人張懷素通謀，誅死。

translations.literal: Anshi's son Chu and Anch's son Mou, both Outer Section Vice Directors, were executed for conspiring with the sorcerer Zhang Huaisu.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's son Chu and Anch's son Mou, both Outer Section Vice Directors, were executed for conspiring with the sorcerer Zhang Huaisu.

sentences.zh: 王珪，字禹玉，成都華陽人，後徙舒。

translations.literal: Wang Gui, styled Yuyu, was a man of Huayang in Chengdu Prefecture; later his family moved to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, styled Yuyu, was a native of Huayang in Chengdu Prefecture; later his family moved to Shu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖永，事太宗為右補闕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yong served Emperor Taizong as Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yong served Emperor Taizong as Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 吳越納土，受命往均賦，至則悉除無名之算，民皆感泣。

translations.literal: When Wuyue submitted to the throne, he was dispatched to equalize tax assessments; upon arrival he abolished all nameless levies, and the people wept with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyue submitted to the throne, he was dispatched to equalize tax assessments. Upon arrival he abolished all nameless levies, and the people wept with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 使還，或言其多弛賦租。

translations.literal: On returning from his mission, someone reported that he had relaxed tax collections too greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission, someone reported that he had relaxed tax collections too greatly.

sentences.zh: 帝詰之，對曰：「使新附之邦，蒙天子仁恩，臣雖得罪，死不恨。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned him; he replied: "To let a newly attached domain receive the Son of Heaven's benevolence—even if I am punished, I shall die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him. He replied, "To let a newly attached domain receive the Son of Heaven's benevolence—even if I am punished, I shall die without regret.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 珪弱歲奇警，出語驚人。

translations.literal: From childhood Gui was uncannily sharp; his words astonished people.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Gui was uncannily sharp, and his words astonished people.

sentences.zh: 從兄琪讀其所賦，唶曰：「騏驥方生，已有千里之志，但蘭筋未就耳。

translations.literal: His elder cousin Qi read what he had composed and clicked his tongue, saying: "A thoroughbred has just been born and already has the will to run a thousand li—only its sinews are not yet formed.
translations.idiomatic: His elder cousin Qi read what he had composed and clicked his tongue, saying, "A thoroughbred has just been born and already has the will to run a thousand li—only its sinews are not yet formed.

sentences.zh: 」舉進士甲科，通判揚州。

translations.literal: " He passed the jinshi in the top cohort and served as Vice Prefect of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He passed the jinshi in the top cohort and served as Vice Prefect of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吏民皆少珪，有大校嫚不謹，捽置之法。

translations.literal: Officials and people alike looked down on Gui for his youth; a senior officer was disrespectful and careless, and Gui seized him and punished him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people alike looked down on Gui for his youth. A senior officer was disrespectful and careless, and Gui seized him and punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 王倫犯淮南，珪議出郊掩擊之，賊遁去。

translations.literal: When Wang Lun invaded Huainan, Gui proposed sortieing beyond the city to strike them in ambush; the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lun invaded Huainan, Gui proposed sortieing beyond the city to strike them in ambush, and the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 召直集賢院，為鹽鐵判官、修起居注。

translations.literal: Summoned to the Hall for Gathering Worthies, he served as Salt and Iron Judge and Compiler of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the Hall for Gathering Worthies, he served as Salt and Iron Judge and Compiler of the Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 接伴契丹使，北使過魏，舊皆盛服入。

translations.literal: Escorting a Khitan envoy, when the northern envoys passed Wei, formerly all wore full court dress to enter.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting a Khitan envoy, when the northern envoys passed Wei, formerly all wore full court dress to enter.

sentences.zh: 至是，欲便服，妄云衣冠在後乘。

translations.literal: This time they wished to wear everyday dress, falsely claiming their caps and robes were in the carriage behind.
translations.idiomatic: This time they wished to wear everyday dress, falsely claiming their caps and robes were in the carriage behind.

sentences.zh: 珪命取授之，使者愧謝。

translations.literal: Gui ordered them fetched and handed over; the envoys apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Gui ordered them fetched and handed over, and the envoys apologized in shame.

sentences.zh: 遂為賀正旦使。

translations.literal: He then served as envoy to offer New Year's congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as envoy to offer New Year's congratulations.

sentences.zh: 進知制誥、知審官院，為翰林學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: Promoted to Drafting Officer for Proclamations and Director of the Bureau of Appointments; Hanlin Academician and prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Officer for Proclamations and Director of the Bureau of Appointments, then Hanlin Academician and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，除喪，復為學士，兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When his mother died he entered mourning; after the mourning period he again became Academician, concurrently Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning. After the mourning period he again became Academician, concurrently Academician Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 先是，三聖並侑南郊，而溫成廟享獻同太室。

translations.literal: Previously, the Three Sage-Emperors were jointly honored at the Southern Suburban sacrifice, while sacrifices at the Wen Cheng temple were offered alongside those in the Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Three Sage-Emperors were jointly honored at the Southern Suburban sacrifice, while sacrifices at the Wen Cheng temple were offered alongside those in the Grand Chamber.

sentences.zh: 珪言：「三后並配，所以致孝也，而瀆乎饗帝。

translations.literal: Gui said: "The joint honoring of the three sage sovereigns is meant to express filial piety, yet it profanes the rites for feasting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "Jointly honoring the three sage sovereigns is meant to express filial piety, yet it profanes the rites for feasting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 後宮有廟，所以廣恩也，而僭乎饗親。

translations.literal: An inner-palace temple is meant to spread grace broadly, yet it oversteps the rites for feasting kin.
translations.idiomatic: An inner-palace temple is meant to spread grace broadly, yet it oversteps the rites for feasting kin.

sentences.zh: 」於是專以太祖侑于郊，而改溫成廟為祠殿。

translations.literal: " Thereupon only Taizu was honored at the suburban sacrifice, and the Wen Cheng temple was changed to a shrine hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon only Taizu was honored at the suburban sacrifice, and the Wen Cheng temple was changed to a shrine hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐立皇子，中書召珪作詔，珪曰：「此大事也，非面受旨不可。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, when an heir was to be established, the Secretariat summoned Gui to draft the edict; Gui said: "This is a great matter—it cannot be done without receiving the charge face to face.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiayou era, when an heir was to be established, the Secretariat summoned Gui to draft the edict. Gui said, "This is a great matter—it cannot be done without receiving the charge face to face.

sentences.zh: 」明日請對，曰：「海內望此舉久矣，果出自聖意乎？

translations.literal: " The next day he requested audience and said: "The realm has long awaited this measure—was it truly the emperor's own intent?
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he requested audience and said, "The realm has long awaited this measure—was it truly the emperor's own intent?

sentences.zh: 」仁宗曰：「朕意決矣。

translations.literal: " Emperor Renzong said: "My mind is decided.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Renzong said, "My mind is decided.

sentences.zh: 」珪再拜賀，始退而草詔。

translations.literal: " Gui bowed twice in congratulation and only then withdrew to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui bowed twice in congratulation and only then withdrew to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修聞而歎曰：「真學士也。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu heard of this and sighed: "A true Academician."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu heard of this and sighed, "A true Academician."

sentences.zh: 」帝宴寶文閣，作飛白書分侍臣，命珪識歲月姓名。

translations.literal: The emperor banqueted at the Hall of Glorious Literature, made flying-white calligraphy to distribute among attending ministers, and ordered Gui to inscribe the date and names.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor banqueted at the Hall of Glorious Literature, made flying-white calligraphy to distribute among attending ministers, and ordered Gui to inscribe the date and names.

sentences.zh: 再宴群王，又使為序，以所御筆、墨、箋、硯賜之。

translations.literal: At a second banquet for the imperial princes he again had Gui compose the preface, bestowing upon him the emperor's own brush, ink, paper, and inkstone.
translations.idiomatic: At a second banquet for the imperial princes he again had Gui compose the preface, bestowing upon him the emperor's own brush, ink, paper, and inkstone.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，當撰先帝諡，珪言：「古者賤不誄貴，幼不誄長，故天子稱天以誄之，制諡於郊，若云受之於天者。

translations.literal: When Yingzong succeeded, the posthumous title of the previous emperor was to be drafted; Gui said: "In antiquity the base did not eulogize the noble, the young did not eulogize the elder—therefore the Son of Heaven proclaimed Heaven when granting the posthumous title, fixing the eulogy at the suburban altar, as if receiving it from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong succeeded, the posthumous title of the previous emperor was to be drafted. Gui said, "In antiquity the base did not eulogize the noble, the young did not eulogize the elder—therefore the Son of Heaven proclaimed Heaven when granting the posthumous title, fixing the eulogy at the suburban altar, as if receiving it from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 近制，唯詞臣撰議，庶僚不得參聞，頗違稱天之義。

translations.literal: Under recent practice only academicians draft the deliberation, and other officials may not take part—this greatly violates the meaning of proclaiming Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Under recent practice only academicians draft the deliberation, and other officials may not take part—this greatly violates the meaning of proclaiming Heaven.

sentences.zh: 請令兩制共議。

translations.literal: I request that both academicians of the two bureaus deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: I request that both academicians of the two bureaus deliberate together.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 濮王追崇典禮，珪與侍從、禮官合議宜稱皇伯，三夫人改封大國，執政不以為然。

translations.literal: On the elevated rites for Prince Pu, Gui together with attendants and ritual officials jointly deliberated that he should be styled Imperial Uncle; the three consorts should be re-enfeoffed as consorts of great states—the chief administration did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: On the elevated rites for Prince Pu, Gui together with attendants and ritual officials jointly deliberated that he should be styled Imperial Uncle and the three consorts re-enfeoffed as consorts of great states—the chief administration did not agree.

sentences.zh: 其後三夫人之稱，卒如初議。

translations.literal: In the end the titles of the three consorts followed the original proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the titles of the three consorts followed the original proposal.

sentences.zh: 始，珪之請對而作詔也，有密譖之者。

translations.literal: At the start, when Gui had requested audience to draft the heir edict, someone had secretly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start, when Gui had requested audience to draft the heir edict, someone had secretly slandered him.

sentences.zh: 英宗在位之四年，忽召至蘂珠殿，傳詔令兼端明殿學士，錫之盤龍金盆，諭之曰：「秘殿之職，非直器卿於翰墨間，二府員缺，即出命矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yingzong's reign, he was suddenly summoned to Ruizhu Hall; an edict was transmitted appointing him concurrently Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity, and he was granted a coiled-dragon gold basin. The emperor told him: "The post in the Secret Hall is not merely to park you among brush and ink—when a vacancy arises in the Two Departments, an appointment will follow at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yingzong's reign he was suddenly summoned to Ruizhu Hall. An edict was transmitted appointing him concurrently Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity, and he was granted a coiled-dragon gold basin. The emperor told him, "The post in the Secret Hall is not merely to park you among brush and ink—when a vacancy arises in the Two Departments, an appointment will follow at once.

sentences.zh: 曩有讒口，朕今釋然無疑。

translations.literal: There was slander before; I am now entirely free of doubt.
translations.idiomatic: There was slander before, but I am now entirely free of doubt.

sentences.zh: 」珪謝曰：「非陛下至明，臣死無日矣。

translations.literal: " Gui thanked him, saying: "Were it not for Your Majesty's supreme clarity, I would soon be dead.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui thanked him, saying, "Were it not for Your Majesty's supreme clarity, I would soon be dead.

sentences.zh: 」神宗即位，遷學士承旨。

translations.literal: " When Shenzong succeeded, he was promoted to Academician-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shenzong succeeded, he was promoted to Academician-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 珪典內外制十八年，最為久次，嘗因展事齋宮，賦詩有所感，帝見而憐之。

translations.literal: Gui had drafted inner and outer edicts for eighteen years—the longest tenure of anyone—and once, performing rites at the fasting palace, composed a poem moved by his feelings; the emperor saw it and took pity on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had drafted inner and outer edicts for eighteen years—the longest tenure of anyone. Once, performing rites at the fasting palace, he composed a poem moved by his feelings, and the emperor saw it and took pity on him.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, appointed Vice Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining he was appointed Vice Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 九年，進同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, promoted to Grand Counselor, Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Grand Academician at the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Grand Counselor, Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Grand Academician at the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，由禮部侍郎超授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng bureaucracy was implemented, he was promoted directly from Vice Minister of Rites to Silver Light Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng bureaucracy was implemented, he was promoted directly from Vice Minister of Rites to Silver Light Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 五年，正三省官名，拜尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎，以蔡確為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with the formal titles of the Three Departments established, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs concurrent with Vice Director of the Chancellery; Cai Que was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, with the formal titles of the Three Departments established, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs concurrent with Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Cai Que was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 先是，神宗謂執政曰：「官制將行，欲新舊人兩用之。

translations.literal: Previously, Emperor Shenzong had told the chief administrators: "When the new bureaucracy is implemented, I wish to use men of old and new together.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Emperor Shenzong had told the chief administrators, "When the new bureaucracy is implemented, I wish to use men of old and new together.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「御史大夫，非司馬光不可。

translations.literal: He also said: "For Censor-in-Chief, no one but Sima Guang will do."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "For Censor-in-Chief, no one but Sima Guang will do."

sentences.zh: 」珪、確相顧失色。

translations.literal: " Gui and Que looked at each other, their faces turning pale.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui and Que looked at each other, their faces turning pale.

sentences.zh: 珪憂甚，不知所出。

translations.literal: Gui was deeply worried and did not know what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was deeply worried and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 確曰：「陛下久欲收靈武，公能任責，則相位可保也。

translations.literal: Que said: "Your Majesty has long wished to recover Lingzhou; if you can take responsibility, your chancellorship can be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Que said, "Your Majesty has long wished to recover Lingzhou. If you can take responsibility for it, your chancellorship can be preserved."

sentences.zh: 」珪喜，謝確。

translations.literal: " Gui was pleased and thanked Que.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui was pleased and thanked Que.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗欲召司馬光，珪薦俞充帥慶，使上平西夏策。

translations.literal: The emperor once wished to summon Sima Guang; Gui recommended Yu Chong to command Qing Prefecture and present a plan to pacify Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wished to summon Sima Guang. Gui recommended Yu Chong to command Qing Prefecture and present a plan to pacify Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 珪意以為既用兵深入，必不召光，雖召，將不至。

translations.literal: Gui thought that since troops had already been sent deep into campaign, Guang would certainly not be summoned—and even if summoned, would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Gui reckoned that with troops already committed to a deep campaign, Guang would certainly not be summoned—and even if summoned, would not come.

sentences.zh: 已而光果不召。

translations.literal: Before long, Guang indeed was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Guang indeed was not summoned.

sentences.zh: 永樂之敗，死者十餘萬人，實珪啟之。

translations.literal: The disaster at Yongle cost more than a hundred thousand lives—it was truly Gui who set it in motion.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster at Yongle cost more than a hundred thousand lives—and it was Gui who had set it in motion.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝有疾，珪白皇太后，請立延安郡王為太子。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor fell ill; Gui informed the Empress Dowager and requested that the Prince of Yan'an be installed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor fell ill. Gui informed the Empress Dowager and requested that the Prince of Yan'an be installed as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子立，是為哲宗。

translations.literal: The heir was installed—this was Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was installed—this was Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 進珪金紫光祿大夫，封岐國公。

translations.literal: Gui was promoted to Grand Master of Golden Casque and Cyan Luster and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was promoted to Grand Master of Golden Casque and Cyan Luster and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 五月，卒於位，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he died in office, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he died in office, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 特輟朝五日，賻金帛五千，贈太師，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: The court was specially suspended for five days; five thousand in gold and silk was granted for funeral expenses; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Wengong, "Cultured and Reverent."
translations.idiomatic: The court was specially suspended for five days. Five thousand in gold and silk was granted for funeral expenses, and he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Wengong, "Cultured and Reverent."

sentences.zh: 賜壽昌甲第。

translations.literal: He was granted a premier residence in Shouchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a premier residence in Shouchang.

sentences.zh: 從父 罕

translations.literal: Paternal uncle: Han
translations.idiomatic: Paternal uncle: Han

sentences.zh: 罕，字師言，以蔭知宜興縣。

translations.literal: Han, styled Shiyan, entered office by privilege as magistrate of Yixing County.
translations.idiomatic: Han, styled Shiyan, entered office by privilege as magistrate of Yixing County.

sentences.zh: 縣多湖田，歲訴水，輕重失其平。

translations.literal: The county had many lakeside fields; each year people petitioned over flooding, and assessments of severity and leniency lost their fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The county had many lakeside fields, and each year people petitioned over flood damage—but assessments of severity lost their fairness.

sentences.zh: 罕躬至田處，列高下為圖，明年訴牒至，按圖示之，某戶可免，某戶不可免，眾皆服。

translations.literal: Han went in person to the fields, charted high and low ground in a map; the next year when petitions arrived, he showed them the map—this household could be exempted, that one could not—and everyone was satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Han went in person to the fields and charted high and low ground in a map. The next year when petitions arrived, he showed them the map—this household could be exempted, that one could not—and everyone was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹在潤，奏下其式于諸道。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan, serving in Run Prefecture, memorialized to distribute his method to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan was serving in Run Prefecture, he memorialized to distribute his method to all circuits.

sentences.zh: 西方用兵，仍年科箭羽于東南，價踴貴，富室至豫貯以待鬻。

translations.literal: With war in the west, arrow-feathers were levied year after year from the southeast; prices soared, and wealthy households even stockpiled them in advance to sell.
translations.idiomatic: With war in the west, arrow-feathers were levied year after year from the southeast. Prices soared, and wealthy households even stockpiled them in advance to sell.

sentences.zh: 罕白郡守，倍其直市之，而令民輸錢。

translations.literal: Han told the prefect to buy them at double the price on the market and have the people pay in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Han told the prefect to buy them at double the market price and have the people pay in cash.

sentences.zh: 旁州聞之，皆願如常州法。

translations.literal: Neighboring prefectures heard of this and all wished to follow Changzhou's method.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring prefectures heard of this and all wished to follow Changzhou's method.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部判官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Associate Administrator of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Associate Administrator of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 修太宗別廟，中貴人大慮材，將一新之。

translations.literal: When the separate shrine to Emperor Taizong was being renovated, a palace eunuch greatly overestimated the materials needed and was about to replace everything anew.
translations.idiomatic: When the separate shrine to Emperor Taizong was being renovated, a palace eunuch greatly overestimated the materials needed and was about to replace everything anew.

sentences.zh: 罕白是特歲久丹漆黯暗，但當致飾耳，榱櫨皆如故，唯易一楹，省緡錢十萬。

translations.literal: Han said it was merely that after years the lacquer and cinnabar had dimmed and only needed refurbishing; beams and rafters were all as before—only one pillar was replaced, saving a hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Han said it was merely that after years the lacquer and cinnabar had dimmed and only needed refurbishing. Beams and rafters were all as before—only one pillar was replaced, saving a hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 出為廣東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Fiscal Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Fiscal Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 儂智高入寇，罕行部在潮，廣州守仲簡自圍中遣書邀罕，罕報曰：「吾家亦受困，非不欲歸，顧獨歸無益，當求所以相濟者。

translations.literal: When Nong Zhigao raided, Han was on inspection tour in Chao Prefecture; the Guangzhou prefect Zhong Jian, trapped in the siege, sent a letter inviting Han. Han replied: "My family is also besieged—not that I do not wish to return, but returning alone would be of no use; I must find some way to help each other."
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao raided, Han was on an inspection tour in Chao Prefecture. The Guangzhou prefect Zhong Jian, trapped in the siege, sent a letter inviting Han in. Han replied, "My family is also besieged—not that I do not wish to return, but returning alone would do no good. I must find some way we can help each other."

sentences.zh: 」遂還惠州。

translations.literal: " He then returned to Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He then returned to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 州之惡少年正相率為盜，里落驚擾，惠人要罕出城，及郊，遮道求救護者數千計。

translations.literal: Ruffian youths in the prefecture were just then banding together as robbers; villages were thrown into alarm. The people of Huizhou wanted Han to leave the city, and when he reached the suburbs, several thousand blocked the road begging protection.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffian youths in the prefecture were banding together as robbers, and villages were thrown into alarm. The people of Huizhou wanted Han to leave the city, and when he reached the suburbs, several thousand blocked the road begging for protection.

sentences.zh: 罕擇父老可語者問以策，曰：「吾屬皆有田客，欲給以兵，使相保聚。

translations.literal: Han chose among the village elders someone he could speak with and asked for a plan; the man said: "We all have tenant farmers; we wish to supply them with arms so they can guard and gather together."
translations.idiomatic: Han chose among the village elders someone he could speak with and asked for a plan. The man said, "We all have tenant farmers—we wish to supply them with arms so they can guard and gather together."

sentences.zh: 」罕曰：「有田客者如是，得矣，無者奈何？

translations.literal: " Han said: "For those with tenant farmers, that will do—but what of those who have none?"
translations.idiomatic: " Han said, "For those with tenant farmers, that will do—but what of those who have none?"

sentences.zh: 」乃呼耆長發里民，補壯丁，每長二百人；

translations.literal: " He then summoned senior elders to mobilize villagers, supplementing strong young men—two hundred per elder;
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned senior elders to mobilize villagers and supplement strong young men—two hundred per elder;

sentences.zh: 又令邑尉增弓手二千。

translations.literal: He also ordered the district magistrate to add two thousand bowmen.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the district magistrate to add two thousand bowmen.

sentences.zh: 巳時下令，約申而集。

translations.literal: He issued orders at the si hour, with assembly set for the shen hour.
translations.idiomatic: He issued orders at si hour (about 9–11 a.m.), with assembly set for shen hour (about 3–5 p.m.).

sentences.zh: 募有方略者，許以官秩、金帛，使為甲首。

translations.literal: He recruited men with stratagems, promising them rank and gold and silk, to serve as squad leaders.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited men with stratagems, promising them rank and gold and silk, to serve as squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 久之，無至者。

translations.literal: After a long while, none came.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, none came.

sentences.zh: 有婦人訴為僕奪釵珥，捕得之，並執奪攘者十八輩，皆梟首決口置道左，傳曰：「此耆長發為壯丁不肯行者也。

translations.literal: A woman came to complain that a servant had robbed her hairpins and earrings; when the thief was caught, eighteen bandits who had been seizing goods were seized as well—all were beheaded and their mouths slit, the bodies placed on the left of the road with a placard: "These are the strong young men whom the senior elders mobilized but who refused to march."
translations.idiomatic: A woman came to complain that a servant had robbed her hairpins and earrings. When the thief was caught, eighteen bandits who had been seizing goods were seized as well—all were beheaded and their mouths slit, the bodies placed on the left of the road with a placard reading, "These are the strong young men whom the senior elders mobilized but who refused to march."

sentences.zh: 」觀者始有怖色。

translations.literal: " Onlookers at last showed fear.
translations.idiomatic: " Onlookers at last showed fear.

sentences.zh: 至期，得六百人，尉所部亦至。

translations.literal: When the deadline came, six hundred men were gathered, and the magistrate's troops arrived as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the deadline came, six hundred men had gathered, and the magistrate's troops arrived as well.

sentences.zh: 於是染庫帛為旗；

translations.literal: Thereupon they dyed treasury silks into flags;
translations.idiomatic: They dyed treasury silks into flags;

sentences.zh: 授之。

translations.literal: and distributed them.
translations.idiomatic: and distributed them.

sentences.zh: 割牛革為盾形，柔之湯中，每盾削竹簽十六，穿於革，以木為鼻，使持之自蔽。

translations.literal: They cut oxhide into shield shapes, softened it in hot water; for each shield sixteen bamboo splints were whittled, pierced through the hide, with a wooden grip so each man could hold it to shield himself.
translations.idiomatic: They cut oxhide into shield shapes and softened it in hot water. For each shield sixteen bamboo splints were whittled and pierced through the hide, with a wooden grip so each man could hold it to shield himself.

sentences.zh: 斷苦竹數千，銛其末，使操為兵。

translations.literal: They cut several thousand bitter bamboo poles, sharpened the tips, and had men wield them as weapons.
translations.idiomatic: They cut several thousand bitter bamboo poles, sharpened the tips, and had men wield them as weapons.

sentences.zh: 悉出公私戎器。

translations.literal: All public and private military gear was brought out.
translations.idiomatic: All public and private military gear was brought out.

sentences.zh: 檄告屬城，仿而行之。

translations.literal: He sent proclamations to subordinate prefectures ordering them to follow suit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent proclamations to subordinate prefectures ordering them to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 數日，眾大振，向之惡少年，皆隸行伍，無敢動。

translations.literal: Within days morale surged greatly; the ruffian youths of before were all enrolled in the ranks and dared not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Within days morale surged. The ruffian youths of before were all enrolled in the ranks and dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 乃簡卒三千，方舟建旗，伐鼓作樂，順流而下。

translations.literal: He then selected three thousand soldiers, linked boats and raised flags, beat drums and played music, and sailed downstream.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected three thousand soldiers, linked boats and raised flags, beat drums and played music, and sailed downstream.

sentences.zh: 將至廣，悉眾登岸，斬木為鹿角，積高數仞，營于南門。

translations.literal: As they neared Guangzhou, he landed his entire force, cut trees into chevaux-de-frise piled several ren high, and encamped at the South Gate.
translations.idiomatic: As they neared Guangzhou, he landed his entire force, cut trees into chevaux-de-frise piled several ren high, and encamped at the South Gate.

sentences.zh: 智高戴黃蓋臨觀，相去三十步，見已嚴備，不敢犯。

translations.literal: Zhigao, beneath a yellow canopy, watched from afar; they were thirty paces apart. Seeing preparations complete, he did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao watched from beneath a yellow canopy; they were thirty paces apart. Seeing the defenses complete, he did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 罕徐開門而入，智高遂解去。

translations.literal: Han slowly opened the gate and entered; Zhigao then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Han slowly opened the gate and entered, and Zhigao then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時南道郵驛斷絕，罕上事，不得通；

translations.literal: At the time southern-route couriers were cut off; Han's memorials could not get through;
translations.idiomatic: At the time southern-route couriers were cut off, and Han's memorials could not get through;

sentences.zh: 而提點刑獄鮑軻遁處南雄，數具奏。

translations.literal: while Judicial Intendant Bao Ke had fled to Nanxiong and repeatedly submitted full reports.
translations.idiomatic: while Judicial Intendant Bao Ke had fled to Nanxiong and repeatedly submitted full reports.

sentences.zh: 及賊平，軻受賞，罕謫監信州酒。

translations.literal: When the bandits were suppressed, Ke received rewards while Han was demoted to superintendent of Xin Prefecture's wine monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were suppressed, Ke received rewards while Han was demoted to superintendent of Xin Prefecture's wine monopoly.

sentences.zh: 安撫使孫沔言罕實有功，復以為西路轉運使。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Sun Mian said Han had truly rendered service, and he was restored as Fiscal Commissioner of the Western Route.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Sun Mian said Han had truly rendered service, and he was restored as Fiscal Commissioner of the Western Route.

sentences.zh: 或傳智高不死，走火峒，儂宗旦據險聚眾，邕守蕭注謀擊之。

translations.literal: Some reported that Zhigao had not died but fled to Huotong; Nong Zongdan held difficult terrain and gathered a crowd; Yongzhou prefect Xiao Zhu planned to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Some reported that Zhigao had not died but fled to Huotong, where Nong Zongdan held difficult terrain and gathered followers. Yongzhou prefect Xiao Zhu planned to attack.

sentences.zh: 罕呼宗旦子日新謂之曰：「汝父內為交阯所仇，外為邊將希賞之餌，非計也。

translations.literal: Han summoned Zongdan's son Rixin and said to him: "Your father is hated within by Jiaozhi and without serves as bait for border generals seeking rewards—this is no wise course.
translations.idiomatic: Han summoned Zongdan's son Rixin and said to him, "Your father is hated within by Jiaozhi and without serves as bait for border generals seeking rewards—this is no wise course.

sentences.zh: 汝歸報，擇利而為之。

translations.literal: Return and report: choose what is advantageous and act on it."
translations.idiomatic: Return and report to him—choose what is advantageous and act on it."

sentences.zh: 於是父子俱降。

translations.literal: Thereupon father and son both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon father and son both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 徙知潭州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部、度支副使，復為潭州。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Ministries of Revenue and of Public Works, he again served as prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Ministries of Revenue and of Public Works, he again served as prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政務適人情，不加威罰。

translations.literal: In governing he strove to suit human feelings and did not impose heavy punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In governing he strove to suit human feelings and did not impose heavy punishments.

sentences.zh: 有狂婦數訴事，出言無章，卻之則勃罵，前守每叱逐之。

translations.literal: There was a mad woman who repeatedly petitioned over matters; her speech was incoherent, and if turned away she would fly into curses—the previous prefect always shouted and drove her off.
translations.idiomatic: There was a mad woman who repeatedly petitioned over matters. Her speech was incoherent, and if turned away she would fly into curses—the previous prefect always shouted and drove her off.

sentences.zh: 罕獨引至前，委曲徐問，久稍可曉，乃本為人妻，無子，夫死，妾有子，遂逐婦而據家資，屢訴不得直，因憤恚發狂。

translations.literal: Han alone brought her forward and gently questioned her at length; gradually it became intelligible. She had originally been a man's wife without children; when her husband died, a concubine had a son and drove the wife out to seize the family property. She had petitioned repeatedly without justice and, from anger and resentment, had gone mad.
translations.idiomatic: Han alone brought her forward and gently questioned her at length until her story gradually became clear. She had originally been a wife without children; when her husband died, a concubine who had a son drove her out and seized the family property. She had petitioned repeatedly without justice and, from anger and resentment, had gone mad.

sentences.zh: 罕為治妾而反其資，婦良愈，郡人傳為神明。

translations.literal: Han punished the concubine and restored the property to the wife; the woman recovered fully, and people in the prefecture spread word of him as a divine official.
translations.idiomatic: Han punished the concubine and restored the property to the wife. The woman fully recovered, and people in the prefecture spread word of him as a divine official.

sentences.zh: 監司上治狀，敕書褒諭，賜絹三百。

translations.literal: Supervisory officials submitted a report on his governance; an imperial letter praised and commended him, granting three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory officials submitted a report on his governance. An imperial letter praised and commended him, granting three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 徙知明州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以光祿卿卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 兄之子珪少孤，罕教養有恩，後珪貴，每予書，必以盛滿為戒云。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Gui was orphaned young; Han raised and nurtured him with kindness. Later, when Gui rose high, whenever Han wrote to him he always warned against fullness and excess.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son Gui was orphaned young, and Han raised and nurtured him with kindness. Later, when Gui rose high, whenever Han wrote to him he always warned against fullness and excess.

sentences.zh: 從兄 琪

translations.literal: Paternal cousin: Qi
translations.idiomatic: Paternal cousin: Qi

sentences.zh: 琪，字君玉，兒童時已能為歌詩。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Junyu, could already compose songs and poems as a child.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, styled Junyu, could already compose songs and poems as a child.

sentences.zh: 起進士，調江都主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 上時務十二事，請建義倉，置營田，減度僧，罷鬻爵，禁錦綺、珠貝，行鄉飲、籍田，復制科，興學校。

translations.literal: He submitted twelve proposals on affairs of the age, asking to establish charity granaries, set up garrison farms, reduce excess monks, abolish the sale of offices, ban brocade, silk gauze, pearls, and cowries, conduct village drinking ceremonies and the plowing ceremony, restore the special examination, and promote schools.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted twelve proposals on affairs of the age: establish charity granaries, set up garrison farms, reduce excess monks, abolish the sale of offices, ban brocade, silk gauze, pearls, and cowries, conduct village drinking ceremonies and the plowing ceremony, restore the special examination, and promote schools.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉之，除館閣校勘、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong commended this and appointed him Collation Officer in the Hall of Literature and Collator in the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong commended this and appointed him Collation Officer in the Hall of Literature and Collator in the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

sentences.zh: 帝宴太清樓，命館閣臣作《山水石歌》，琪獨蒙褒賞。

translations.literal: The emperor banqueted at Taiping Tower and ordered academicians to compose "Song of Landscape and Stone"; Qi alone received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor banqueted at Taiping Tower and ordered academicians to compose "Song of Landscape and Stone." Qi alone received commendation.

sentences.zh: 詔通判舒州。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as vice prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as vice prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奏發廩救民，未報，先振以公租，守以下皆不聽，琪挺身任之。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he memorialized to open the granaries to aid the people; before a reply came, he advanced public rent grain first—the prefect and those below all refused, but Qi personally assumed responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he memorialized to open the granaries to aid the people. Before a reply came, he advanced public rent grain first—the prefect and those below all refused, but Qi personally assumed responsibility.

sentences.zh: 知復州，民毆佃客死，吏論如律。

translations.literal: As prefect of Fu Prefecture, when a commoner beat a tenant farmer to death, the clerks judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Fu Prefecture, when a commoner beat a tenant farmer to death, the clerks judged according to law.

sentences.zh: 琪疑之，留未決，已而新制下，凡如是者聽減死。

translations.literal: Qi was doubtful and held the case undecided; soon a new statute was issued—wherever such cases occurred, reduced death sentences were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was doubtful and held the case undecided. Soon a new statute was issued permitting reduced death sentences in such cases.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官，直集賢院、兩浙淮南轉運使、修起居注、鹽鐵判官、判戶部勾院、知制誥。

translations.literal: He served in turn as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, Academician directly attached to the Hall for Gathering Worthies, Fiscal Commissioner of the Two Zhe and Huai circuits, compiler of the Veritable Records, Salt Monopoly Commissioner, Reviewer of the Ministry of Revenue registry, and Draftsman of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, Academician directly attached to the Hall for Gathering Worthies, Fiscal Commissioner of the Two Zhe and Huai circuits, compiler of the Veritable Records, Salt Monopoly Commissioner, Reviewer of the Ministry of Revenue registry, and Draftsman of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 嘗入對便殿，帝從容謂曰：「卿雅有心計，若三司缺使，當無以易卿。」

translations.literal: Once, entering audience in the Informal Hall, the emperor said gently: "You are naturally shrewd in planning—if the Three Departments should lack a commissioner, no one should replace you."
translations.idiomatic: Once, entering audience in the Informal Hall, the emperor said gently, "You are naturally shrewd in planning—if the Three Departments should lack a commissioner, no one should replace you."

sentences.zh: 會奉使契丹，因感疾還，上介誣其詐，責信州團練副使。

translations.literal: Just then he was sent as envoy to Khitan; he returned ill, and a senior envoy falsely accused him of feigning sickness, for which he was demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Just then he was sent as envoy to Khitan. He returned ill, and a senior envoy falsely accused him of feigning sickness, for which he was demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Xin.

sentences.zh: 久之，以龍圖閣待制知潤州。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Awaiting Draftsman at the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and prefect of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was made Awaiting Draftsman at the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and prefect of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 轉運使欲浚常、潤漕河，琪陳其不便，詔寢役。

translations.literal: The fiscal commissioner wished to dredge the Chang and Run transport canals; Qi set forth the drawbacks, and an edict halted the project.
translations.idiomatic: The fiscal commissioner wished to dredge the Chang and Run transport canals. Qi set forth the drawbacks, and an edict halted the project.

sentences.zh: 而後議者卒請廢古城埭，破古函管而浚之，河反狹，舟不得方行，公私交病。

translations.literal: But later the advocates finally petitioned to abandon the old city weir, break the ancient sluice gates and dredge—and the river became narrower instead; boats could not sail abreast, and public and private interests alike suffered.
translations.idiomatic: But later the advocates finally petitioned to abandon the old city weir, break the ancient sluice gates, and dredge—and the river became narrower instead. Boats could not sail abreast, and public and private interests alike suffered.

sentences.zh: 徙知江寧。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 先是，府多火災，或託以鬼神，人不敢救。

translations.literal: Previously the prefecture had suffered many fires; some attributed them to spirits and ghosts, and people dared not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the prefecture had suffered many fires. Some attributed them to spirits and ghosts, and people dared not rescue.

sentences.zh: 琪召令廂邏，具為作賞捕之法，未幾，得奸人，誅之，火患遂息。

translations.literal: Qi summoned the ward patrol leaders and fully established reward-and-capture regulations; before long the culprits were caught and executed, and the fires ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Qi summoned the ward patrol leaders and fully established reward-and-capture regulations. Before long the culprits were caught and executed, and the fires ceased.

sentences.zh: 復知制誥，加樞密直學士、知鄧州，徙揚州，入判太常寺，又出知杭州，復為揚州、潤州。

translations.literal: He again served as Draftsman of Edicts, was made Academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Dengzhou, transferred to Yangzhou, entered as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, went out again as prefect of Hangzhou, and again served at Yangzhou and Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Draftsman of Edicts, was made Academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Dengzhou, transferred to Yangzhou, entered as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, went out again as prefect of Hangzhou, and again served at Yangzhou and Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: He retired as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 琪性孤介，不與時合。

translations.literal: Qi was by nature solitary and upright, ill suited to his times.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was by nature solitary and upright, ill suited to his times.

sentences.zh: 數臨東南名鎮，政尚簡靜。

translations.literal: He repeatedly governed famous posts in the southeast; his administration favored simplicity and calm.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly governed famous posts in the southeast, and his administration favored simplicity and calm.

sentences.zh: 每疾俗吏飾廚傳以沽名譽，故待賓客頗闊略。

translations.literal: He always resented vulgar officials who lavishly stocked kitchens and lodges to buy reputation, and so his reception of guests was rather sparse.
translations.idiomatic: He always resented vulgar officials who lavishly stocked kitchens and lodges to buy reputation, and so his reception of guests was rather sparse.

sentences.zh: 間造飛語起謗，終不自恤。

translations.literal: From time to time slander was fabricated against him, yet he never looked after himself.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time slander was fabricated against him, yet he never looked after himself.

sentences.zh: 葬於真州。

translations.literal: He was buried in Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔真、揚二州發卒護其窆，蓋異數也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhen and Yang prefectures to dispatch soldiers to escort his interment—an extraordinary honor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhen and Yang prefectures to dispatch soldiers to escort his interment—an extraordinary honor.

sentences.zh: 論曰：公亮靜重鎮浮，練達典憲，與韓琦並相，號稱老成。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Gongliang was calm and weighty, restraining the frivolous; thoroughly versed in statutes and precedents—as co-chancellor with Han Qi he was called mature and steady.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Gongliang was calm and weighty, restraining the frivolous, and thoroughly versed in statutes and precedents. As co-chancellor with Han Qi he was called mature and steady.

sentences.zh: 升之自為言官，即著直聲。

translations.literal: Shengzhi, from the time he became a remonstrance official, won a reputation for blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi, from the time he became a remonstrance official, won a reputation for blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 然皆挾術任數，公亮疾琦專任，薦王安石以間之，升之陰助安石，陽為異同，以避清議，二人措慮如此，豈誠心謀國者乎？

translations.literal: Yet all relied on stratagem and scheming. Gongliang resented Qi's monopoly of power and recommended Wang Anshi to divide it; Shengzhi secretly assisted Anshi while openly feigning disagreement to evade pure criticism—the two men's calculations were of this sort. Were they truly men who sincerely sought the state's good?
translations.idiomatic: Yet all relied on stratagem and scheming. Gongliang resented Qi's monopoly of power and recommended Wang Anshi to divide it; Shengzhi secretly assisted Anshi while openly feigning disagreement to evade pure criticism—their calculations were of this sort. Were they truly men who sincerely sought the state's good?

sentences.zh: 新法之行，何望其能正救也。

translations.literal: With the new laws being implemented, how could one expect them to set things right and save the realm?
translations.idiomatic: With the new laws being implemented, how could one expect them to set things right and save the realm?

sentences.zh: 及安石去位，充、珪實代之，天下喁喁，思有所休息。

translations.literal: When Anshi left office, Wu Chong and Gui in truth replaced him; throughout the realm people murmured, longing for some respite.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi left office, Wu Chong and Gui in truth replaced him. Throughout the realm people murmured, longing for some respite.

sentences.zh: 充力不逮心，同僚左掣右伺，至鞅鞅以死，傷哉，其不足與有行也。

translations.literal: Chong's strength did not match his intentions; colleagues pulled from the left and watched from the right, until he died discontented—how sad! He was not equal to carrying reforms through.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's strength did not match his intentions; colleagues pulled from the left and watched from the right, until he died discontented—how sad! He was not equal to carrying reforms through.

sentences.zh: 珪容身固位，于勢何所重輕，而陰忌正人，以濟其患失之謀，鄙夫可與事君也與哉！

translations.literal: Gui preserved himself and held his post; what weight did he carry in the balance of power? Yet he secretly resented upright men to serve his fear of loss—can a base man be entrusted with serving his ruler!
translations.idiomatic: Gui preserved himself and held his post—what weight did he carry in the balance of power? Yet he secretly resented upright men to serve his fear of loss. Can a base man be entrusted with serving his ruler!
